title: The Meaning of La Ilaaha Illa Allah
question: What are the conditions and the true meaning of the testimony of faith?
notes_sources: It means there is no true God but Allah. It must be fulfilled truthfully and sincerely, dedicating all acts of worship solely to Him, and requires love for Allah, His Messenger, and all Muslims [1-3].

title: The Three Aspects of Tawheed
question: What are the three categories of Islamic Monotheism?
notes_sources: 1. Lordship (Rububiyya - Creator and Sustainer), 2. Worship (Uluhiyya - none has the right to be worshipped but Him), 3. Names & Attributes (Asma-was-Sifaat - confirming His attributes without twisting their meanings) [4, 5].

title: The Danger of Polytheism
question: Why is calling upon other than Allah considered the greatest wrongdoing?
notes_sources: It is the greatest Shirk. Calling others for help from the unseen leads to disbelief (Kufr) and cancels good deeds. Paradise and sustenance can be requested from none other than Allah [6].

title: Hidden Polytheism
question: Is it permissible to wear rings, twine, or talismans for protection?
notes_sources: No. To seek refuge in, vow to, or wear talismans/amulets for protection from other than Allah is an act of Shirk [7, 8].

title: The Six Pillars
question: What are the fundamental articles of Faith?
notes_sources: Belief in: 1. Allah, 2. His Angels, 3. His Revealed Books, 4. His Messengers, 5. The Day of Resurrection, 6. Al-Qadr (Divine Decree - the good and bad thereof) [4, 9].

title: The World of Angels
question: What are the specific duties of Jibreel, Mikaaeel, and Israafeel?
notes_sources: Jibreel is in charge of revelation ('life of the heart'), Israafeel blows the trumpet for resurrection ('reviving bodies'), and Mikaaeel is responsible for rain and vegetation ('sources of life') [10].

title: The Divine Decree
question: What are the four levels of belief in Predestination (Qadar)?
notes_sources: 1. Allah's eternal knowledge of everything, 2. Allah has written everything in the Preserved Tablet, 3. Allah's all-encompassing Irresistible Will, 4. Allah is the Creator of all things [11, 12].

title: The Five Pillars
question: What are the five foundational pillars of Islam?
notes_sources: 1. Testimony of Faith, 2. Performing Prayers (5 times daily), 3. Paying Zakat, 4. Fasting Ramadan, 5. Performing Hajj (if capable) [3].

title: The Core Purpose
question: Why did Allah create mankind and jinn?
notes_sources: 'I did not create jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me' (51:56). Worship is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and approves of (prayer, honesty, charity, etc.) [13, 14].

title: Acceptance of Deeds
question: What two conditions must be met for a deed to be accepted by Allah?
notes_sources: 1. Sincerity (done purely for Allah's sake to earn His pleasure). 2. Correctness (done according to the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad) [15-18].

title: The Soul of the Deed
question: Why must deeds be completely free from showing off (Riyaa')?
notes_sources: Allah does not accept a deed shared with another. Ikhlas means stripping oneself of worshipping any besides Allah; it is the exact opposite of associating partners with Him [19-21].

title: Transforming the Mundane
question: How can everyday habits become acts of worship?
notes_sources: A believer with strong intention can transform permissible daily deeds (like sleeping to gain strength to worship, or spending on family) into acts of obedience pleasing to Allah [22-25].

title: Establishing the Prayer
question: What is the difference between 'praying' and 'establishing the prayer'?
notes_sources: Establishing prayer means executing it with proper outward mechanics (Wudhu, timing, congregation) and inward states (diligence, submission, humbleness, calmness) [26, 27].

title: The Pillar of the Religion
question: What is the first matter a person will be held accountable for on the Day of Judgment?
notes_sources: The prayer. If it is sound, the rest of the deeds will be sound. The Prophet warned that abandoning prayer is what separates a person from polytheism and disbelief (Kufr) [28, 29].

title: Preparing for Prayer
question: What are the seven conditions required before starting the prayer?
notes_sources: 1. Islamic faith, 2. Intention, 3. Cleanliness (body/clothes/place), 4. Purification (Wudhu/Ghusl), 5. Concealing the 'Awrah, 6. Facing the Qiblah, 7. Prescribed timing [30-32].

title: Nullifiers of Purity
question: What actions invalidate a person's ablution (Wudhu)?
notes_sources: Passing wind, urinating, defecating, or deep sleep. Note: Passing wind only requires performing a new Wudhu; it does not require washing the private parts (Istinja) [33].

title: The Barrier in Prayer
question: Why is it important to place an object (Sutrah) in front of you while praying?
notes_sources: It acts as a barrier preventing passersby from invalidating or diminishing your prayer. The Prophet commanded stopping anyone who tries to pass between the worshipper and the Sutrah [34-37].

title: Common Prayer Mistakes
question: What are some common physical mistakes people make during prostration (Sujood)?
notes_sources: Failing to prostrate on all seven bones (forehead/nose, two palms, two knees, toes of both feet), raising the feet off the ground, or spreading the arms flat on the floor like a dog [38-40].

title: Presence of Heart
question: How can one maintain focus and solemnity during prayer?
notes_sources: By looking at the place of prostration, avoiding fidgeting, and realizing you are standing before Allah. Looking around is described by the Prophet as Shaytan 'stealing' from the prayer [41-43].

title: Invalidating the Prayer
question: What actions will render a prayer completely invalid?
notes_sources: Talking intentionally, laughing, eating, drinking, uncovering the 'Awrah, turning away from the Qiblah, or failing to observe any of the core pillars of the prayer [44-46].

title: Rectifying Mistakes
question: How do you correct an accidental omission or addition in your prayer?
notes_sources: By performing two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sujuud As-Sahw) at the end of the prayer. If a core pillar was omitted, the pillar itself must first be repeated [45, 47, 48].

title: The Social Pillar
question: Why is paying Zakat a crucial foundation of Islamic society?
notes_sources: It purifies wealth, cleanses the soul of greed, and supports the needy. It is ranked closely with prayer, mentioned alongside it 82 times in the Quran, and secures Allah's mercy [49].

title: The School of Self-Restraint
question: What are the main spiritual goals of fasting in Ramadan?
notes_sources: Fasting generates self-restraint, piety, and God-consciousness. A valid fast requires the intention to fast to be made for the sake of Allah prior to dawn [50-52].

title: The Ultimate Journey
question: What is the spiritual reward for an accepted Hajj?
notes_sources: The Prophet said: 'Whoever performs the Hajj for the sake of Allah and does not commit any lewdness or sins returns like the day in which his mother gave him birth' (sinless) [53].

title: Acknowledging the Sunnah
question: Why is the Prophet's Sunnah essential for understanding the Quran?
notes_sources: The Sunnah is the practical explanation of the Quran. The Prophet's life defines the morals and laws of the Quran clearly; turning away from his practice is a rejection of true guidance [54, 55].

title: The Danger of Heresy
question: Why are innovations in religion so dangerous?
notes_sources: Satan loves Bid'ah more than disobedience because people rarely repent from it, falsely thinking they are doing good. 'Whoever does an action which is not from our affair, it is rejected' [56, 57].

title: Supreme Love
question: How much must a believer love the Prophet Muhammad?
notes_sources: Complete faith requires loving him more than one's fathers, sons, wealth, and even one's own self. Emulating his character and following his commands is the ultimate proof of this love [58-60].

title: Taking Account
question: Why should a Muslim perform a daily self-accounting?
notes_sources: To review obligations and voluntary deeds at the end of the day. If there are shortcomings or sins, one must blame themselves, feel remorse, repent, and rectify the evil done [61, 62].

title: The Struggle for Patience
question: What are the three levels of patience in Islam?
notes_sources: 1. Steadfastness in obeying Allah, 2. Steadfastness in avoiding prohibited matters (sins), 3. Patience and restraint at the onset of calamity or hardship [63].

title: The Fire of Anger
question: What physical mechanics did the Prophet teach to overcome anger?
notes_sources: Seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan, keep silent, and change your physical posture (sit down if standing, lie down if sitting) to physically quell the physiological surge of rage [64, 65].

title: Honesty and Integrity
question: What is the true reality of truthfulness?
notes_sources: It is having one's inner state conform exactly to their outer state, devoid of self-conceit or hypocrisy. Allah does not accept any action unless it is done with truthfulness [21, 66-71].

title: Gratitude to Parents
question: Why is being dutiful to parents ranked so highly in Islam?
notes_sources: Allah closely ties good behavior towards parents with the command to worship Him alone. A mother, in particular, has the greatest right to good companionship due to her hardships in childbearing [72-77].

title: Harmony in Marriage
question: What are the shared rights between a husband and wife?
notes_sources: Loyalty, honesty, mutual trust, love, mercy, and general good manners. The Prophet said: 'The best of you is the one who is best to his family' [78-81].

title: Leading the Household
question: What are the primary obligations of a husband towards his wife?
notes_sources: Providing the dower, complete financial maintenance according to his means, treating her honorably, ensuring her sexual fulfillment, and teaching her the religion [82-86].

title: Devotion of the Wife
question: What are the main responsibilities of a wife towards her husband?
notes_sources: Obeying him in matters that do not disobey Allah, protecting his honor and wealth, guarding the household, and not allowing anyone into the house without his permission [87-89].

title: Nurturing the Next Generation
question: What are the fundamental rights of a child in Islam?
notes_sources: Being provided for in a healthy manner, being taught the tenets of the religion, being treated with mercy, impartiality among siblings, and having good examples set by parents [90-92].

title: Equality Among Offspring
question: Why does Islam strictly forbid favoring one child over another?
notes_sources: Favoritism leads to dissension, enmity, and psychological conflict. The Prophet commanded, 'Fear Allah and treat your children fairly,' when a man tried to give a gift to only one of his sons [92, 93].

title: The Bond of Faith
question: Why is Islamic brotherhood stronger than blood ties?
notes_sources: Blood ties are often severed for worldly gain, but ties forged by belief in Allah endure eternally. Believers are like one body; if one limb hurts, the rest of the body suffers sleeplessness and fever [94-97].

title: Obligations to Brethren
question: What are the six obligatory acts of courtesy a Muslim owes another?
notes_sources: 1. Greet them with Salaam, 2. Accept their invitations, 3. Give sincere counsel when asked, 4. Bless them when they sneeze, 5. Visit them when ill, 6. Attend their funeral [98].

title: Dealing with the Creation
question: How should a Muslim behave toward non-Muslims and animals?
notes_sources: With justice, equity, and excellence. Muslims must call non-Muslims to Allah with wisdom, and treat animals mercifully, killing them humanely and without torture if required for consumption [99-101].

title: Integrity in Commerce
question: What destroys the blessing of a business transaction?
notes_sources: Concealing facts, lying, or artificially inflating prices. Honesty and straightforwardness are the keys to a blessed transaction that benefits both parties in this world and the Hereafter [102-104].

title: The Catastrophe of Wealth
question: Why does Islam take such a firm stance against usury/interest?
notes_sources: It is an appetite hidden in the lower self that seeks easy money without effort or risk, destroying the social fabric and exploiting the needy. The Prophet equated it to a heinous, destructive crime [105, 106].

title: Guarding the Senses
question: Why does the Quran emphasize lowering the gaze?
notes_sources: Lowering the gaze blocks the entrance of Shaytan, protects the private parts, and purifies the heart from illicit sexual desires which lead to societal ruin and the wrath of Allah [107, 108].

title: The Deception of the World
question: How can excessive love for wealth and children become a trial?
notes_sources: If they distract a believer from fulfilling their duties to Allah or pursuing the truth. Wealth and children are a test, and ultimate success lies in preferring the eternal reward of the Hereafter [60, 109-112].

title: Remembering the Inevitable
question: How does remembering death benefit the believer?
notes_sources: It crushes worldly attachments, encourages urgent repentance, and focuses the mind on preparing for the eternal life to come. Death is the doorway every soul must eventually pass through [113, 114].

title: The Ultimate Questions
question: What happens to the soul immediately after burial?
notes_sources: Two angels make the person sit up and ask: 'Who is your Lord?', 'What is your Deen?', 'Who is your Prophet?' The believer answers truthfully and receives a glimpse of Paradise, while the hypocrite doubts [115-117].

title: The Day of Justice
question: What occurs on the Day of Judgment?
notes_sources: Mankind will be resurrected to stand before their Lord. No one will be wronged, and true success will be having one's deeds weighed, removing oneself from the Fire, and entering Paradise [118, 119].

title: The Abode of Bliss
question: How is the physical beauty of Paradise described?
notes_sources: Its soil is musk and saffron, its rocks are pearls, and its buildings are bricks of gold and silver. It contains things no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no mind has imagined [120-122].

title: The Supreme Reward
question: What is the absolute greatest delight for the people of Paradise?
notes_sources: Gazing upon the Face of Allah. It is a pleasure of the heart that completely surpasses all physical delights of Paradise, like rivers, mansions, or fruits [123-125].

title: The Examples of Greatness
question: Why is it crucial to study the lives of the Prophet's Companions?
notes_sources: They represent the highest pinnacle of faith, sacrifice, and loyalty. Following their example is the best way to understand how the Quran and Sunnah are practically applied [126-133].

title: Sincere Advice
question: Why did the Prophet say 'The religion is Naseehah (sincere advice)'?
notes_sources: It embodies every virtue. It means sincerity to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and the common folk, ensuring justice and truth prevail throughout the Ummah [134].

title: Advising with Wisdom
question: How should a Muslim advise another believer?
notes_sources: Advice should be given with kindness, gentleness, and in private. Exhorting someone in public is considered scolding and humiliation rather than sincere advice [135].

title: Healing the Heart
question: What is the reward and etiquette for reciting the Quran?
notes_sources: It should be recited with reflection and understanding. It acts as an intercessor on the Day of Judgment, opening blind eyes and locked hearts, and serving as a light in this world [136, 137].

title: Reaping the Fruits of Knowledge
question: Why is acquiring Islamic knowledge mandatory?
notes_sources: Seeking knowledge atones for sins. However, knowledge without practice is fruitless; a scholar must practice what they preach to truly benefit themselves and others [138, 139].

title: Polishing the Soul
question: How does Dhikr impact the heart of the believer?
notes_sources: Dhikr polishes the heart, removes the rust of heedlessness, and brings one closer to Allah. The Prophet called those who engage in abundant Dhikr 'the Mufarridoon' who take the lead [140, 141].

title: The Gardens of Jannah
question: What happens when Muslims gather to remember Allah?
notes_sources: Angels surround them, mercy descends upon them, and Allah mentions them to those with Him. The Prophet called these gatherings the 'gardens of Jannah' on earth [142].

title: Guarding the Tongue
question: What are the dangers of unrestricted speech?
notes_sources: Talking too much or joking excessively weakens one's honor, instills hatred, and hardens the heart. The Prophet said: 'Whoever remained silent, gained salvation' [143, 144].

title: The Etiquette of Greeting
question: Who should initiate the greeting of peace (Salaam)?
notes_sources: The one who is closer to Allah precedes in saying Salaam. A complete greeting involves a warm smile and a physical handshake, which completes the courtesy [145, 146].

title: Visiting the Sick
question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a sick Muslim?
notes_sources: It is one of the foundational rights of a Muslim. The visitor is enveloped in mercy, and it serves as an opportunity to ask the sick person for supplications, as they are close to Allah's mercy [147, 148].

title: The Best of Generations
question: What made the generation of the Prophet the greatest?
notes_sources: The Prophet said, 'The best people are those living in my generation.' They were unswerving in their faith, supported the Messenger, and sacrificed their wealth and lives for Islam [126, 130].

title: Steps of Wudhu
question: What are the essential acts of Wudhu (ablution)?
notes_sources: The essential acts include washing the entire face (including rinsing the mouth and nostrils), washing both arms up to the elbows, wiping the whole head from hairline to the nape, and washing both feet up to the ankles [1], [2]. These must be done in the correct sequence and continuously without unnecessary pauses [1].

title: Nullifiers of Wudhu
question: What invalidates a person's Wudhu?
notes_sources: Wudhu is invalidated by passing wind, urinating, defecating, deep sleep, or losing consciousness [1], [2]. If a person simply passes wind, they do not need to wash their private parts (Istinja); they only need to perform a new Wudhu [3], [4].

title: Dry Ablution
question: When is Tayammum (dry ablution) permissible?
notes_sources: Tayammum is permitted when water is completely unavailable, when acquiring it is too difficult or expensive, or when using water would cause physical harm or severe illness due to extreme cold [5], [6], [7].

title: Wiping Over Socks
question: How long can a traveler or resident wipe over their leather socks for Wudhu?
notes_sources: The Prophet established the limit for wiping over leather socks as three days and nights for a traveler, and one day and one night for a resident [7]. The wiping must be done over the top of the sock, not the bottom [8].

title: Establishing the Prayer
question: What does it mean to truly 'establish' the prayer?
notes_sources: Establishing the prayer goes beyond mere physical movements; it requires executing it with proper outward mechanics and inward states like diligence, humility, and submission [9]. It is the prayer of the heart and soul, standing silently in fear of Allah [10].

title: The Opening Takbeer
question: Why is the opening Takbeer critical to the prayer?
notes_sources: Takbeerat-ul-Ihraam (saying 'Allahu Akbar' to start) initiates the prayer. If omitted, the entire prayer must be repeated [11]. The Prophet said the key to prayer is purification, it is entered by Takbeer, and exited by Tasleem [12], [13].

title: The Sutrah
question: What is the Sutrah and why is it used?
notes_sources: The Sutrah is an object placed in front of the worshipper to act as a barrier [14]. It should be approximately a handspan or two above the ground, and it protects the prayer from being invalidated if someone or something passes in front [15], [16], [17].

title: The Perfect Prostration
question: Which seven body parts must touch the ground during Sujuud?
notes_sources: The Prophet commanded prostration on seven bones: the forehead (including the nose), both palms, both knees, and the toes of both feet [18], [19], [20]. Raising the feet invalidates the prostration [21], [22].

title: The Sitting of Rest
question: How should one sit between the two prostrations?
notes_sources: One should spread the left leg and sit on it (Iftiraash), while keeping the right foot upright with the toes pointing to the Qiblah [23]. One must sit at ease until every bone and vertebra returns to its place [23], [24].

title: The Tashahhud
question: What is recited during the sitting of the Tashahhud?
notes_sources: The worshipper recites praises to Allah, sends peace upon the Prophet, peace upon the righteous slaves, and testifies that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger [25]. In the final Tashahhud, sending prayers (Salawat) upon the Prophet is obligatory [26], [27].

title: Humility in Prayer
question: How does a worshipper achieve Khushu' in prayer?
notes_sources: Khushu' requires the stillness of limbs and a heart completely focused on Allah [28]. The worshipper should look at the place of prostration and avoid looking around, as looking around is a 'snatching away' that Shaytan steals from the prayer [29], [30], [31].

title: Tranquility in Action
question: Why is rushing through the prayer dangerous?
notes_sources: The absence of ease and tranquility invalidates the prayer entirely [32]. The Prophet commanded a man who prayed hastily to repeat his prayer, teaching him that a worshipper must not move to the next pillar until his bones settle at ease in the current position [32], [33].

title: Congregational Prayer
question: How important is praying in congregation for men?
notes_sources: Establishing prayer in the congregation is obligatory for men unless there is a valid legislative excuse [34]. The Prophet strongly warned those who hear the call to prayer but fail to respond by coming to the mosque [35].

title: Prostration of Forgetfulness
question: How do you correct omissions in your prayer?
notes_sources: If a necessary duty (like a specific Takbeer) is missed unintentionally, it is rectified by making two additional prostrations at the end of the prayer [36], [37]. However, if a core pillar is omitted, the missed pillar itself must be repeated first [37], [38].

title: The Danger of Missing Prayer
question: What is the ruling on intentionally abandoning prayer?
notes_sources: Abandoning the prayer is what separates a person from polytheism and disbelief [39], [40]. The Companions did not consider the abandonment of any deed to be disbelief except the abandonment of prayer [41].

title: Timing of Prayers
question: What is the consequence of delaying prayer past its time?
notes_sources: Prayers are enjoined at fixed, prescribed hours [42]. Delaying them past their prescribed time without a valid excuse is a major sin. Intentionally waiting until the sun is setting to quickly rush through it resembles the prayer of the hypocrite [41], [43].

title: Testification of Faith
question: What does testifying that 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah' entail?
notes_sources: It means believing in what he informed us, obeying his commands, avoiding what he prohibited, and worshiping Allah only in the manner he prescribed [44]. It affirms he is a slave of Allah, not a divine being possessing the power to bring ultimate harm or benefit [44].

title: The True Meaning of Shirk
question: Why is Shirk the only unforgivable sin?
notes_sources: Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is a great wrongdoing because it diverts worship to beings that do not deserve it [45]. Allah forgives anything less than Shirk for whom He wills, but forbids Paradise to those who die committing it [45], [46].

title: Seeking Help from the Dead
question: Is it permissible to supplicate to inhabitants of graves?
notes_sources: Seeking help from the dead, supplicating to them, or requesting their assistance is major Shirk [47]. Turning to graves for assistance or sacrificing animals for them associates partners with Allah, contradicting the command to worship Him alone [48], [47], [49].

title: Minor Shirk
question: What actions constitute minor shirk?
notes_sources: Swearing by other than Allah (like swearing by one's honesty or a trust) is minor shirk [50], [51]. Hanging an amulet for protection is also minor shirk, unless the person believes the object itself creates the benefit/harm, which escalates it to major shirk [52].

title: Extremism in Reverence
question: Why does Islam forbid exaggerating the status of righteous people?
notes_sources: Exaggerating the status of prophets or righteous people to the point of deifying them removes a person from the fold of Islam [53]. The Quran specifically warns against exceeding limits in religion, as seen in the case of Jesus, son of Maryam [54].

title: Innovation in Religion
question: Why are innovations (Bid'ah) rejected in Islam?
notes_sources: The Prophet warned that any action introduced into the religion that is not part of the established legislation will be rejected [55], [56]. Specifying certain days or months for worship without proof from the Sunnah falls under this category [57].

title: Belief in Al-Qadr
question: Does predestination mean we shouldn't strive?
notes_sources: No. Using Qadr (Divine Decree) as an excuse to abandon striving or justify sins is severe misguidance [58], [59], [60]. A believer must take the means to an end, trusting that Allah has decreed both the outcomes and the causes leading to them [61].

title: The Compassion of the Prophet
question: How did the Prophet treat children?
notes_sources: He was incredibly merciful and playful. Once, while leading prayer, his grandson Al-Husayn climbed on his back during prostration. The Prophet extended the prostration to avoid rushing the child until he finished playing [62], [63].

title: Resembling the Prophet
question: Which Companion closely resembled the Prophet physically?
notes_sources: Al-Hasan ibn Ali bore a striking resemblance to the Prophet from his chest to his head [64]. The Prophet deeply loved him, called him a 'sayyid' (leader), and declared him one of the leaders of the youth in Paradise [65], [66].

title: The Reconciler
question: How did Al-Hasan fulfill the Prophet's prophecy?
notes_sources: The Prophet prophesied that Al-Hasan would reconcile two great groups of Muslims [67]. He achieved this by voluntarily yielding the Caliphate to Mu'awiyah, prioritizing the unity of the Ummah and the preservation of Muslim blood over worldly power [68], [69].

title: Asceticism of Ahl al-Bayt
question: What was the lifestyle of 'Ali and Fatimah?
notes_sources: They lived a life of patience and striving, often facing severe hunger and manual labor [70], [71]. Even when worldly treasures were available later, 'Ali remained ascetic and prioritizing the Hereafter [72].

title: The Power of Patience
question: What are the two forces within a human regarding patience?
notes_sources: Every person has a 'driving force' pushing them towards actions, and a 'restraining force' holding them back [73]. Patience harnesses the driving force for good deeds and the restraining force to prevent harmful or sinful actions [73].

title: Types of Patience
question: What is the difference between patience by choice and enforced patience?
notes_sources: Patience by choice (e.g., actively refraining from sin) is of a higher spiritual status than enforced patience (e.g., enduring an illness you cannot control), as enforced patience is common to all, while chosen patience requires strong faith [74].

title: Patience in Sickness
question: How should a Muslim react to illness?
notes_sources: A sick person must submit to Allah's decree without complaining against Him [75]. Enduring illness with patience obliterates sins. One should never wish for death or commit suicide due to the pain, but rather hope for Allah's mercy [76], [77].

title: Lowering the Gaze
question: Why is lowering the gaze a cure for forbidden desires?
notes_sources: The eyes are the gateway to the heart. Continually looking at forbidden things exposes the heart to fatal arrows of temptation [78], [79]. Lowering the gaze blocks Shaytan and protects the heart from distraction and spiritual ruin [80], [79].

title: Taming the Stomach
question: How does the amount of food we eat affect our spiritual health?
notes_sources: The stomach is the root of sickness. Eating to excess provides fuel for lower appetites like lust, making the soul rebellious [81], [82]. The Prophet advised filling only a third of the stomach with food, a third with drink, and leaving a third for breath [81].

title: Reliance on Allah
question: How does trusting Allah remove anxiety?
notes_sources: Believing that whatever Allah decrees is ultimately good for the believer brings immense peace to the heart [83]. Knowing that what missed you could never have afflicted you, and what afflicted you could never have missed you, cures worry and distress [84], [85].

title: Avoiding 'If Only'
question: Why did the Prophet warn against saying 'If only...'?
notes_sources: Saying 'If only I had done this...' opens the door for Shaytan's whispers, breeding regret and grief over the past [85]. Instead, a believer should say, 'Allah decreed and did what He willed,' accepting the outcome with contentment [85].

title: Remembrance of Death
question: Why should a believer constantly remember death?
notes_sources: Remembering death destroys the illusions of worldly pleasures, crushes worldly attachments, and cures the rust of the heart [86], [87]. The Prophet advised living in this world like a stranger or a traveler shading himself briefly under a tree [88].

title: The Sweat of the Gathering
question: What happens to mankind on the Day of Judgment?
notes_sources: People will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, and the sun will be brought so close that people will be drenched in their own sweat. The level of sweat—whether up to the knees, waist, or mouth like a bridle—will depend on their deeds [89].

title: The Testimony of the Limbs
question: How will a person's own body testify against them?
notes_sources: On the Day of Judgment, mouths will be sealed, and hands, feet, and skin will speak and bear witness to the deeds they committed. Allah, who gives speech to all things, will grant them the ability to speak [90].

title: The Hideousness of Hellfire
question: How is the physical punishment in Hell described?
notes_sources: The inhabitants of the Fire will have layers of fire covering them from above and below [91]. The physical size of a disbeliever will be magnified immensely—with a molar tooth the size of Mount Uhud—so they may fully taste the severity of the torment [91].

title: The Beauty of Paradise
question: What are the physical traits of the people of Paradise?
notes_sources: They will enter Jannah aged thirty-three, hairless on their bodies, and tall like their father Adam (sixty cubits) [92]. They will not suffer illness, bodily waste, or aging, and their garments will never wear out [93], [92].

title: The Homes in Paradise
question: What are the dwellings in Jannah made of?
notes_sources: Believers will have palaces made of gold, jewels, and pearls [94], [95]. There are transparent apartments whose inside can be seen from the outside, specially prepared for those who fast, feed the poor, and pray at night while others sleep [96], [97].

title: The Market of Paradise
question: What happens when the inhabitants of Paradise gather?
notes_sources: They will visit a market where a cloud of white musk will shower beautiful fragrances upon them [98, 99]. When they return to their spouses, their beauty and radiance will have increased significantly in the eyes of their partners [100].

title: The Ultimate Delight
question: What is the absolute greatest reward in Paradise?
notes_sources: The absolute greatest delight is gazing upon the Face of Allah [101, 102]. The believers will see Him as clearly as one sees the full moon on a cloudless night, a joy that completely surpasses all other heavenly pleasures [103].

title: Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil
question: What is the consequence of abandoning the command to forbid evil?
notes_sources: Allah praised the Muslim Ummah for enjoining right and forbidding wrong [104]. Showing apathy towards this duty can incur the curse and punishment of Allah, as happened to previous nations (like the Children of Israel) who ignored evil actions within their societies [104], [105].

title: Extravagance and Waste
question: What is the Islamic stance on wasting food and wealth?
notes_sources: Extravagance is strictly prohibited; Allah does not love those who waste [106]. Pouring away usable food or drink is a belittlement of Allah's favors. Believers are commanded to consume moderately and share with those who are hungry [106], [107].

title: Visiting the Sick
question: What are the spiritual benefits of visiting someone who is ill?
notes_sources: It establishes deep love and affection in the heart of the invalid [108]. The visitor should bring happiness to the sick person, prolong the visit if desired, and remind them gently to repent without causing anxiety or fear [109], [110].

title: Supplications for the Sick
question: What should a Muslim say when visiting the sick?
notes_sources: The Prophet taught specific supplications asking Allah, the Lord of the people, to remove the illness, as He is the only Healer whose cure leaves no ailment behind [111], [112]. Reciting Surah Al-Fatihah is also a powerful form of Ruqyah (healing) [113].

title: The Danger of Tale-Carrying
question: What is the punishment for spreading malicious gossip (Namimah)?
notes_sources: The Prophet stated clearly that the tale-carrier will not enter Paradise [114]. Spreading lies and carrying tales to cause hatred and division between people is a major sin that leads to severe punishment in the grave [114].

title: Keeping Family Ties
question: Why is maintaining family ties essential?
notes_sources: Keeping ties of kinship prolongs one's lifespan and increases provision [115]. Severing ties is a major sin that brings Allah's curse, blinding the sight and deafening the ears to the truth [115].

title: Financial Dealings
question: Can you sell something you do not currently own?
notes_sources: No. The Prophet explicitly forbade selling goods that one does not physically possess or own [116], [117]. Merchants must learn the rules of buying and selling to avoid falling into impermissible transactions or usury (Riba) [118], [119].

title: False Oaths in Business
question: What happens when a seller uses false oaths to sell goods?
notes_sources: Using false oaths to convince a buyer removes the divine blessing (Barakah) from the transaction [120]. It is a grave sin that ultimately destroys the spiritual and material benefit of the wealth earned [121], [118].

title: The Friday Prayer (Jumu'ah)
question: What actions are prohibited during the Friday sermon?
notes_sources: Talking while the Imam is delivering the sermon, fidgeting with clothes, phones, or pebbles, and stepping over people's necks to find a spot are all prohibited and ruin the reward of Jumu'ah [122], [123].

title: Fasting Ramadan
question: Does fasting only require abstaining from food and drink?
notes_sources: No. Fasting requires abstaining from idle and obscene speech [124]. If someone insults a fasting person, they should simply reply, 'I am fasting.' Engaging in sins ruins the spiritual purpose and reward of the fast [124].

title: Paying Zakat
question: What is the warning for those who hoard wealth and refuse to pay Zakat?
notes_sources: Refusing to pay Zakat is a major sin. Hoarded gold and silver will be heated in the Fire of Hell and used to brand the foreheads, flanks, and backs of the hoarders on the Day of Resurrection [125], [126].

title: Rulings of Hajj
question: Can one wear sewn garments while in the state of Ihram?
notes_sources: A male pilgrim in Ihram is prohibited from wearing stitched garments tailored to the limbs, like shirts or pants [127]. Violating the prohibitions of Ihram out of apathy is a sin [128].

title: Stoning the Jamarat
question: Do the stones thrown at the Jamarat physically hit Shaytan?
notes_sources: No. The Jamarat mark the places where Shaytan appeared to Prophet Ibrahim, but Shaytan is not physically standing there today [129]. It is an act of worship to remember Allah, and the stones do not need to be washed prior to throwing [130].

title: Celebrating Innovated Holidays
question: Is it permissible to celebrate non-Muslim holidays?
notes_sources: Participating in or celebrating non-Muslim holidays (like New Year's or Mother's Day) is prohibited. It constitutes imitating the disbelievers in matters specific to them, which the Prophet strictly forbade [131], [132].

title: Cursing and Insulting
question: Is it allowed to curse animals, the weather, or other creations?
notes_sources: The Prophet forbade insulting anyone or anything, including animals, diseases, and time [133], [134]. This is because Allah is the Creator and ultimate Controller of all affairs and creations [134].

title: The Etiquette of Sleeping
question: How should a Muslim prepare for sleep and wake up?
notes_sources: One should recite specific words of remembrance (Dhikr), blow into the hands after reciting the last three Surahs, and wipe the body to seek protection [135], [136]. Upon waking, one should thank Allah for restoring life after the 'minor death' of sleep [137].

title: The Rights of Brotherhood
question: What are the basic rights a Muslim owes to another?
notes_sources: A Muslim owes obligatory acts of courtesy: greeting with Salaam, accepting invitations, giving sincere advice when asked, blessing them when they sneeze, visiting them when ill, and attending their funeral [138], [139].

title: The Best of People
question: Who is considered the best of people in the sight of Allah?
notes_sources: The best of people is the one who lives a long life and uses it to perform good, righteous deeds [140]. Ultimately, the most honorable in the sight of Allah is the one who has the most Taqwa (piety and God-consciousness) [141], [142].

title: Leftover Water of Animals
question: Is water that an animal has drunk from considered pure?
notes_sources: Water left in a container after an 'allowable' animal (one whose meat is permissible to eat) has drunk from it is pure, as its saliva qualifies for consumption [1]. Water remaining in a pot after it has been drunk from by a donkey, mule, beasts, or birds of prey is also considered pure and permissible for ablution [1].

title: The Impurity of Dogs
question: How should a container licked by a dog be cleansed?
notes_sources: Dogs are considered impure [2]. Any container that a dog has licked must be washed seven times, with the first washing being done with dirt, until the water mixed with dirt becomes muddy [2].

title: Small Quantities of Unclean Water
question: When does water become permanently unclean?
notes_sources: If any impurities are mixed with a small quantity of water (defined as less than 2 Qullas), then this water is considered definitively unclean, regardless of whether or not there is a relative change in its taste, color, or odor [3].

title: The Danger of Appetites
question: What happens when human appetites are given free rein?
notes_sources: An appetite is the desire of the lower self to obtain something which it imagines will satisfy it or give it enjoyment [4]. If the appetites are given free rein, people will continually seek more and more of what will ultimately lead them to destruction by making them overstep limits and leave the right path [4].

title: Moderating Food Intake
question: How much food should a Muslim consume?
notes_sources: The Prophet Muhammad taught that a human being does not fill any vessel worse than his stomach [5]. Enough for the son of Adam are a few morsels to keep his back straight; if it cannot be avoided, then a third of the stomach is for food, a third is for drink, and a third is left empty for breath [5].

title: Etiquette Before Eating
question: What should a Muslim intend and do before eating?
notes_sources: A Muslim should try to make his food and drink pure by preparing them from permissible, lawful sources [6]. The intention behind eating should be to strengthen oneself for the purpose of worshipping Allah, which transforms the permissible act of eating into an act of worship that is rewarded by Allah [6].

title: Etiquette While Eating
question: What are the proper manners to observe while eating?
notes_sources: A person should begin his meal by saying 'In the name of Allah' [7]. He should eat with three fingers of his right hand, take small portions, chew well, and eat the food that is close to him rather than taking from the middle of the plate [7]. A Muslim should also lick his fingers clean before wiping or washing them [8].

title: Etiquette After Eating
question: How should a believer conclude a meal?
notes_sources: A person should stop eating before becoming completely full to avoid debilitating indigestion and gluttony [9]. He must praise Allah after eating or drinking, and it is recommended to pick up whatever food has fallen as an act of thankfulness for Allah's bounties [9].

title: Sunnahs of Drinking Water
question: How did the Prophet instruct Muslims to drink water?
notes_sources: One should drink with the right hand while seated and recite Bismillah before drinking [10]. The Prophet forbade drinking water in one breath like a camel; rather, it should be drunk in two or three breaths, separating the glass from the mouth to breathe, and one should say Alhamdulillah after finishing [10], [11].

title: Entering the Homes of Others
question: What is the proper procedure for entering a private house?
notes_sources: A believer must ask permission to enter other people's homes and greet the inhabitants by saying 'Peace be upon you' three times [12], [13]. If no one is home, or if permission is not granted and the person is told to go away, it is an obligation for him to leave immediately [12], [13].

title: Brotherhood and Mutual Support
question: How should believers support one another?
notes_sources: A believer with respect to another believer is like a building, where one part strengthens and reinforces the other [14]. The similitude of believers in their love, mercy, and compassion toward one another is like a body; if one limb is in pain, the rest of the body suffers sleeplessness and fever [14].

title: The Rights of Neighbors
question: How strictly does Islam command good treatment of neighbors?
notes_sources: The Prophet stated that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should be generous to his neighbor and absolutely not harm him [15]. He also mentioned that the Angel Gabriel kept advising him concerning the neighbor to the point that he thought the neighbor would be given a share of inheritance [15].

title: Kindness Towards Animals
question: How should a Muslim treat animals?
notes_sources: A Muslim feeds or gives water to an animal if he finds it hungry or thirsty, knowing there is a divine reward for serving every living creature with a moist liver [16]. The Prophet also cursed anyone who uses a creature with a soul as an archery target, and prohibited tying down animals to kill them [16].

title: Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil
question: What is the duty of a Muslim when witnessing wrongdoing?
notes_sources: The Quran commands that there must be a community among believers who call to the good, enjoin the right, and forbid the wrong [17]. The Prophet instructed that he who sees something objectionable should change it with his hand; if unable, then with his tongue; and if unable, then reject it in his heart, which is the weakest level of faith [18].

title: The Sin of Backbiting
question: Why is backbiting heavily condemned in the Quran?
notes_sources: A Muslim should not backbite, scorn, insult, ridicule, or call another by offensive nicknames [19]. Allah likens the sin of backbiting to the repulsive act of eating the flesh of one's dead brother, emphasizing how deeply it should be hated [19].

title: The Prohibition of Insulting and Cursing
question: What did the Prophet say about those who curse others?
notes_sources: The true believer is not given to insulting, cursing a great deal, obscene talk, or foul speech [20]. Those who curse a great deal will be deprived of being martyrs or intercessors on the Day of Resurrection, and abusing a Muslim is considered a wicked act [20].

title: Upholding the Ties of Kinship
question: What is the consequence of severing family ties?
notes_sources: Maintaining ties of kinship results in reward, increased provisions, and a prolonged lifespan [21]. The womb is suspended from the Divine Throne, declaring that whoever connects it, Allah will connect them, and whoever severs it, Allah will sever him [22].

title: Modesty in Clothing
question: What types of clothing are strictly prohibited for Muslims?
notes_sources: For men, dragging the garment below the ankles out of arrogance is forbidden, as Allah does not love those who drag their garments [23]. Furthermore, wearing tight, transparent, or flimsy clothing that reveals the 'awrah (private areas) in front of people is prohibited [23].

title: Gold and Silver Vessels
question: Can Muslims eat or drink from expensive gold or silver plates?
notes_sources: It is strictly impermissible to drink from vessels made of gold or silver, or to eat from plates made of such materials [24]. The Prophet warned that whoever drinks from vessels of gold or silver is only gulping fire from Hellfire into his stomach [24].

title: Lowering the Gaze
question: How does Islam protect society from unlawful sexual temptations?
notes_sources: Believing men and women are commanded by Allah to lower their eyes and strictly guard their private parts [25]. Watching visual media or looking at things that reveal the 'awrah of men or women is prohibited in order to safeguard one's religion and purity [26].

title: The Abomination of Intoxicants
question: Why does Islam strictly forbid alcohol and drugs?
notes_sources: Alcohol, gambling, and intoxicants of all kinds are declared an abomination of Satan's handiwork [27]. Intoxicants deaden intellectual abilities, leading to misguidance, bad habits, and the disruption of personal and societal life, opening the door to further deviations [28].

title: The Catastrophe of Usury (Riba)
question: How severe is the sin of consuming interest (Riba)?
notes_sources: Usury is a heinous crime against which Islam takes a firm stance, as it is nourished by the greedy love of easy wealth [29]. The Prophet cursed anyone who consumes usury, gives it, records it, or witnesses it, equating it to incredibly grave sins like a man having intercourse with his mother [30], [31].

title: The Sin of Hoarding
question: What is the punishment for a merchant who hoards food to inflate prices?
notes_sources: The Prophet warned that if anyone hoards staple grain for forty days, he has washed his hands of Allah and Allah has washed His hands of him [32]. Foodstuffs must not be withheld from people to artificially raise prices [32].

title: Misappropriation and Theft
question: What is the consequence of stealing public or private property?
notes_sources: Consuming another's property by false means or misappropriating public funds (ghulul) is strictly forbidden [33]. Whoever misappropriates anything will carry that very burden on their neck in total disgrace on the Day of Rising [34], [35].

title: Tampering with Weights and Measures
question: How does Islam view stinting in commercial transactions?
notes_sources: Giving short weight or measure is a hidden form of theft and a foul disease that causes societal imbalance and injustice [36], [37]. Allah warns of a terrible woe for those who demand full measure for themselves but hand over less when weighing for others [36].

title: The Evil of Fornication
question: Why does Allah explicitly command not to even 'go near' fornication?
notes_sources: Fornication is a grave indecent act and an evil way [38]. When someone commits it, the halter of Islam slips from his neck, and their faces will be burned with fire on the Day of Rising unless they sincerely repent [39], [40].

title: Patience in Sickness
question: How should a Muslim react when struck by illness?
notes_sources: A Muslim should be contented with what Allah has predestined and patiently bear the sickness [41]. He should praise Allah, seek reward for the affliction, and understand that Allah ultimately replaces the hardship with something better for the patient believer [41].

title: Crying vs. Wailing over the Dead
question: Is it permissible to cry when a loved one dies?
notes_sources: Weeping gently over a deceased person is permitted both before and after death [42]. However, wailing (Niyaahah)—which includes shrieking, striking the cheeks, and tearing clothes—is strictly forbidden as it reflects the ignorant practices of Jahiliyyah and discontent with Allah's decree [43], [44].

title: At the Point of Death
question: What should be done for a person in the throes of death?
notes_sources: Those present should encourage the dying person to pronounce the Shahaadah ('Laa ilaaha illallaah') so it is their last word [45]. They should also earnestly supplicate for them and only speak good words in their presence [45].

title: Washing the Deceased
question: Who should wash the dead body, and how?
notes_sources: Washing the deceased is a communal obligation (Fard Kifaayah) [46]. Men should be washed by men, and women by women; the washing should be done an odd number of times using water and sidr (lote tree leaves), keeping the body covered with a sheet [47], [48].

title: Shrouding the Deceased
question: How is a Muslim shrouded for burial?
notes_sources: The shroud must be paid for from the deceased's own wealth, even if it exhausts it [49]. It is sunnah to shroud a male in three white cotton cloths that are rolled up to cover the whole body, without using a tailored shirt or turban [49], [50].

title: The Funeral Procession
question: What is the etiquette for following a funeral bier?
notes_sources: It is a right of a Muslim to have his funeral procession followed, which is prescribed for men and not women [51], [52]. Participants should hasten with the procession without running, and strictly avoid loud weeping, carrying incense, or engaging in un-Islamic customs [52].

title: The Funeral Prayer
question: What are the mechanics of the funeral prayer (Salatul Janaazah)?
notes_sources: It is a Fard Kifaayah consisting of four takbeers [53], [54]. After the first takbeer, Al-Fatihah is recited silently; after the second, salawat is sent upon the Prophet; after the third, sincere supplication is made for the deceased; and after the fourth, a tasleem is given [55], [56].

title: Burial Regulations
question: How should the body be placed in the grave?
notes_sources: The body should be entered into the grave from the foot of the grave [57]. It must be placed on its right side with its face turned towards the Qiblah, while the person placing it recites: 'With the name of Allah and upon the Sunnah of Allah's Messenger' [57], [58].

title: Giving Condolences
question: What is the Sunnah method of consoling the grieving family?
notes_sources: Relatives should be encouraged to have patience and await the promise of reward [59]. However, gathering formally in a specific place to receive condolences or expecting the grieving family to prepare food for guests are innovations to be avoided [60].

title: Benefiting the Deceased
question: What actions of the living can benefit someone who has died?
notes_sources: A deceased person continues to benefit from Muslims supplicating for them, the payment of their outstanding debts, the carrying out of any fasts they had vowed, the righteous actions of their children, and any continuing charity or knowledge they left behind [61], [62].

title: Visiting the Graves
question: What is the correct purpose of visiting a graveyard?
notes_sources: Visiting graves is permissible specifically to take admonition, remember the Hereafter, and to greet and supplicate for the deceased [62], [63]. It is strictly forbidden to seek aid from the dead, build structures over graves, or sacrifice animals there [62], [64].

title: The Islamic Will
question: Why is it important to write an Islamic Will?
notes_sources: To settle outstanding debts and rights, and because many people are overcome by religious innovations regarding funerals, it is a duty upon the Muslim to explicitly order in his will that he be prepared and buried strictly according to the Sunnah [65].

title: The Angel of Death
question: What happens at the exact moment of death?
notes_sources: The Angel of Death comes to take the soul [66]. If it is the soul of a believer, the angel gives it to the angels of mercy who welcome it with peace, but if it is an unbeliever, it is harshly given to the angels of punishment [67].

title: The Questioning in the Grave
question: What questions are asked immediately after burial?
notes_sources: After burial, two angels will come, make the deceased sit up, and ask three fundamental questions: 'Who is your Lord?', 'What is your deen (religion)?', and 'Who is this man who was sent amongst you (Muhammad)?' [68], [69].

title: Punishment and Bliss in the Grave
question: Do souls experience reward or torture before Judgment Day?
notes_sources: Yes, the righteous believer will have a door to Paradise opened for them, bringing its fragrance and expanding the grave [70]. Conversely, the unbeliever or hypocrite who cannot answer the angels will be struck with an iron hammer, and their grave will compress until their ribs are crushed together [71], [72].

title: The Trumpet and Resurrection
question: How will the Day of Rising begin?
notes_sources: The Trumpet will be blown, causing all those in the heavens and earth to lose consciousness [73]. When it is blown a second time, everyone will instantly stand upright, resurrected from the coccyx bone, looking on in shock and bewilderment [73], [74].

title: The Sweat of the Gathering
question: What physical trial will mankind face while waiting for Judgment?
notes_sources: The sun will come so close to everyone that it will be as if it is only a mile away [75]. People will be drenched in sweat depending on their worldly actions; for some, the sweat will reach their knees, for others the waist, and some will wear a bridle of sweat reaching their mouths [75].

title: The Testimony of the Limbs
question: How will evidence be brought against sinners?
notes_sources: On the Day of Reckoning, Allah will seal up the mouths of the wrongdoers so they cannot lie [76]. Their own hands, feet, hearing, sight, and skin will be given speech by Allah to bear witness and testify against them concerning what they earned [76].

title: The Balance (Mizan)
question: What exactly will be weighed on the Day of Judgment?
notes_sources: The physical slave themselves, the records and scrolls of their actions, and the actual rewards and forms of their good and bad actions will all be weighed in a true Balance to establish perfect justice [77], [78], [79].

title: Crossing the Sirat
question: What is the Sirat and how will people cross it?
notes_sources: The Sirat is a slippery bridge laid over the Fire of Hell, lined with massive hooks and thorns [80], [81]. The believers will cross it at different speeds depending on their deeds—some like the blink of an eye, lightning, or wind—while others will be snatched and piled up in the Fire [81].

title: The Punishment of Hell
question: What kind of torments await the inhabitants of the Fire?
notes_sources: The unbelievers will be dragged in chains and iron collars [82]. They will have garments of fire cut out for them, boiling water poured over their heads melting their skin and bellies, and they will be beaten with cudgels made of iron [83].

title: Eternity Without Death
question: Will anyone ever die in Paradise or Hell?
notes_sources: Once people are assigned to their final abodes, death will be brought in the visual form of a beautiful sheep and slaughtered between Paradise and Hell [84]. A caller will then announce to both groups that there is only eternity and no more death [84], [85].

title: The Gates of Paradise
question: Will people enter Paradise through specific gates based on their deeds?
notes_sources: Yes, whoever is among the people of prayer will be called from the Gate of Prayer; the people of charity from the Gate of Sadaqa; the people of jihad from the Gate of Jihad; and the people of fasting from the Gate of the Well-Watered (Bab ar-Rayyan) [86].

title: The Food and Drink of Paradise
question: Will the inhabitants of Paradise need to relieve themselves after eating?
notes_sources: The people of the Garden will eat delicious fruit and bird-meat as they desire [87]. However, they will not need to spit, urinate, or defecate; their food will digest simply as a burp and perspiration that smells like beautiful musk [88].

title: The Rivers of Paradise
question: What flows through the rivers of Paradise?
notes_sources: Paradise contains magnificent rivers of water that are forever pure, rivers of milk whose taste never changes, rivers of wine that are a delight without any negative intoxicating effects, and rivers of clarified, pure honey [89], [90].

title: Dress and Ornaments in Paradise
question: How will the believers be adorned?
notes_sources: The people of Paradise will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade [91]. They will be adorned with bracelets of gold and silver, garlands of pearls and rubies, and crowns like those of kings, remaining forever youthful and healthy [92].

title: The Lowest Rank in Paradise
question: What will the last person to enter Paradise receive?
notes_sources: The last man to exit Hell and enter Paradise will be granted by Allah the equivalent of the greatest kingdom of the world, and then ten times more like it, simply out of Allah's immense mercy and generosity [93].

title: The Highest Rank in Paradise (Al-Wasilah)
question: What is Al-Wasilah and who receives it?
notes_sources: Al-Wasilah is the absolute highest rank in Paradise, positioned above all other ranks [94]. It is reserved for only one chosen servant of Allah, which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) confirmed he hopes to be, asking his Ummah to pray he receives it [94].

title: The Day of Increase (More)
question: What special event occurs every Friday in Paradise?
notes_sources: Friday in Paradise is called the 'Day of More'. The inhabitants will gather in a vast valley of white musk, and Allah will descend and invite them to ask Him for whatever they wish, granting them bounties no eye has seen nor ear heard [95], [96].

title: The Great Intercession
question: Who will intercede for humanity when they are waiting for Judgement?
notes_sources: After all other Prophets decline, the Prophet Muhammad will fall prostrate before Allah beneath the Throne until he is given permission to speak [97]. Allah will say, 'Raise your head and speak... intercede, your intercession will be accepted,' allowing him to save vast numbers of his Ummah [97].

title: Rescue from the Fire
question: Will any Muslims be taken out of the Fire?
notes_sources: After the angels, prophets, and believers intercede, Allah the Most Merciful will take a handful from Hell, bringing out people who had turned into charcoal but never associated partners with Him [98]. They will be bathed in the River of Life to heal and then enter Paradise [98].

title: The Greatest Delight: Seeing Allah
question: What is the absolute highest reward for the believers?
notes_sources: The believers will have no doubt in seeing their Lord openly on the Day of Resurrection, just as there is no doubt in seeing the sun at noon or the full moon on a cloudless night [99], [100]. Looking at His Face is a joy that eclipses all other bounties of Paradise [101], [102].

title: Perfection of Sincerity
question: How can a Muslim maximize the reward of permissible daily actions?
notes_sources: The intention of a Muslim is better than his deed [103]. By consciously making multiple good intentions—such as eating to gain strength to worship, recite the Quran, serve parents, or acquire knowledge—a person transforms mundane habits into highly rewarded acts of worship [104].

title: Acknowledging Allah's Favor
question: What is the result of truly recognizing Allah's favors upon oneself?
notes_sources: When a servant deeply acknowledges Allah's continuous favors and grace, they will lavish in the love and intimacy (al-uns) of Allah [105]. This brings profound tranquility, amiability in His company, and an intense longing to meet Him in the Hereafter [105].

title: The Value of Time
question: Why should a Muslim deeply value each passing day?
notes_sources: The Companion Ibn Mas'ud stated: 'I have never regretted anything as much as my regret over a day on which the sun sets and my life span decreases while my good deeds have not increased' [1]. Every sensible person must secure their time to achieve true happiness and righteousness [2].

title: The Foundation of Islam
question: What does it mean that 'The religion is Naseehah'?
notes_sources: The Prophet equated the entire religion to giving Naseehah (sincere advice/sincerity). This sincerity is owed to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and the common folk [3, 4]. It is a way of wishing for your brother what you wish for yourself [5].

title: The Etiquette of Counsel
question: How should a Muslim advise someone who is sinning?
notes_sources: The righteous predecessors always admonished others privately. Exhorting a brother in front of people is merely scolding and humiliating them, whereas giving advice in seclusion achieves the true objective of mending their faults [6].

title: The Universal Key
question: Why is gentleness essential when giving advice?
notes_sources: Gentleness is the best key to unlock a closed heart. The Prophet said: 'Kindness is not to be found in anything but that it adds to its beauty, and it is not withdrawn from anything but it makes it defective' [7].

title: The Barrier to Paradise
question: Why does pride prevent a person from accepting advice?
notes_sources: The Prophet warned that a person with an atom's worth of pride in their heart will not enter Paradise. He defined Kibr as 'to reject the truth, and to despise the people.' An arrogant person rejects advice because they look down upon the advisor, while a humble person accepts the truth regardless of the source [8].

title: The Postures of Anger
question: What should you do physically when you feel enraged?
notes_sources: The Prophet provided a physical cure for the escalation of anger: 'If any of you becomes angry and he is standing, let him sit down... then lie down.' Sitting or lying down minimizes the chance that a person will strike out, break things, or do something crazy that they will later regret [9].

title: The True Measure of Strength
question: How does Islam define a 'strong' person?
notes_sources: True strength is not physical prowess. The Prophet said: 'The strong man is not the one who can overpower others (in wrestling); rather, the strong man is the one who controls himself when he gets angry' [10].

title: Dealing with Ignorance
question: How should a believer respond to foolish or offensive behavior?
notes_sources: The Quran instructs: 'Show forgiveness, enjoin what is good and turn away from the foolish' [11]. By realizing that everyone makes mistakes, a Muslim should cultivate a forgiving and calm character, protecting themselves from being easily provoked [11].

title: Today is All You Have
question: Why should a Muslim focus their energy entirely on 'today'?
notes_sources: 'When you wake up in the morning, do not expect to see the evening.' Your life span is essentially just one day. By focusing on today, you can organize your hours, pray with a wakeful heart, and avoid being caught between the obsession over the past and the anxieties of the future [12].

title: The Past is Gone Forever
question: Why is brooding over past tragedies spiritually harmful?
notes_sources: Brooding over the past is a form of sickness that destroys your resolve for the present. 'Episodes of the past are finished with; sadness cannot retrieve them... This is because the past is non-existent.' A believer must not perform an autopsy on history, but rather move forward [13].

title: Leave the Future Alone
question: Why shouldn't a person obsess over future disasters?
notes_sources: The future belongs to the realm of the unseen, and it has not yet been created. It is foolish to 'pick fruits before they become ripe.' Many anxieties about future poverty or disaster are directly inspired by Shaytan to paralyze the believer [14].

title: How to Deal with Bitter Criticism
question: What is the best reaction to insults from the ignorant?
notes_sources: If you are wounded by their words, you have realized their hopes. Instead, remain firm, forgive them, and show them beautiful manners. A person sitting on the ground cannot fall, and people do not kick a dead dog; criticism often means you have surpassed them in righteousness or success [15, 16].

title: Do Not Expect Gratitude
question: Why shouldn't you be dismayed when people are ungrateful for your help?
notes_sources: Allah created humans to worship Him, yet many are ungrateful to Him, their Creator. If they are ungrateful to the Lord, they will certainly disregard your favors. Perform acts of charity purely seeking Allah's pleasure, and you will be successful regardless of people's ungratefulness [16, 17].

title: Convert a Lemon into a Sweet Drink
question: How does an intelligent believer handle misfortune?
notes_sources: An intelligent person transforms losses into profits, whereas a foolish person makes two disasters out of one. For example, Imam Ahmad emerged from imprisonment and torture as the Imam of the Sunnah. If you are handed a squeezed lemon, look for the bright side and turn it into a sweet drink [18].

title: Do Not Be a Mimicker
question: Why does Islam encourage maintaining your own pure nature?
notes_sources: Do not feign to forget your own voice, movements, or habits to artificially imitate others. From Adam to the last baby, no two people are exactly the same. Go forth according to your own nature and disposition, and cultivate your unique personality based on revelation [19].

title: The Power of a Smile
question: How does a smiling soul differ from a frowning one?
notes_sources: The smiling soul sees difficulties and loves to surmount them. The frowning soul magnifies problems and spends its time justifying failures. Confidence, friendly manners, and a generous smile are vital weapons in overcoming life's obstacles [20].

title: The Six Ingredients of Happiness
question: What are the components to mentally overcome a severe hardship?
notes_sources: A wise person formulated this six-part remedy: 1. Firm trust in Allah; 2. Resigning oneself to the inescapable decree; 3. Knowing patience has no substitute; 4. Unwavering belief that forbearance is essential; 5. Asking 'Why be a party to my own destruction?'; 6. Realizing that from one hour to the next, difficulties vanish [21, 22].

title: Do Not Grieve Over Trivialities
question: How should a believer view the minor annoyances of the world?
notes_sources: The entire world is trivial. A righteous man was once thrown into a lion's cage and saved; when asked what he was thinking about, he said he was pondering whether the lion's saliva was pure or impure. By maintaining lofty aims for the Hereafter, earthly worries lose their power [23, 24].

title: Finding Consolation in the Afflicted
question: How can looking at others ease your own suffering?
notes_sources: Look to the right and left—every house experiences mourning. Find consolation with those who are worse off than you. Realize that your difficulties are tiny compared to those who are bedridden for years, imprisoned, or who have lost their children. Praise Allah that your trial wasn't worse [25].

title: Presence of Mind in Recitation
question: How should the Quran be recited to maximize its benefit?
notes_sources: A person must recite the Quran while pondering over its meaning with due respect and presence of mind. Reciting it while heedless or contradicting its teachings risks inviting the curses mentioned within the verses upon oneself [26].

title: The Supreme Right to Companionship
question: Between parents, who has the most right to your excellent treatment?
notes_sources: The Prophet was asked, 'Who has the most right to my good company?' He answered, 'Your mother.' The man asked again twice, and both times the Prophet said, 'Your mother,' before finally saying 'Your father' on the fourth ask, highlighting her unmatched sacrifice [27].

title: The Mutual Rights of Spouses
question: What is the overarching Quranic rule for marital behavior?
notes_sources: Allah commands: 'And live with them honorably' (Quran 4:19). This fulfills the 'firm and strong covenant' of marriage, requiring mutual respect, liberality, and good treatment under all circumstances [28].

title: Guarding Marital Secrets
question: What is the consequence of exposing intimacy and private marital matters?
notes_sources: The Prophet strictly warned: 'The people in the worst position in Allah's sight on the Day of Resurrection is a man he goes to his wife and she to him and he then spreads her secrets.' A husband and wife must serve as trusted guardians of each other's honor [29].

title: The Reality of Backbiting
question: Does backbiting only apply when you lie about someone?
notes_sources: No. The Prophet defined backbiting (Gheebah) as: 'It is to mention something about your brother that he dislikes.' When the companions asked, 'Even if what you said is truly found in your brother?' He replied, 'If what you said is truly found in him, you have backbitten him' [30].

title: Fulfilling Covenants and Pledges
question: What happens if a person habitually breaks their promises?
notes_sources: Breaking promises is a core trait of hypocrisy. The Prophet said that possessing four traits makes someone a pure hypocrite: acting treacherously in pacts, lying when speaking, breaking promises, and behaving foully in disputes [31].

title: Loving for the Sake of Allah
question: What is the reward for visiting a brother purely for Allah's sake?
notes_sources: A man visited a brother without any worldly motive, blood relation, or desire for bounty. An angel intercepted him and announced: 'Allah has sent me to you informing you that He loves you because you love that man for Allah's sake. Paradise has become obligatory for you' [32].

title: The Rights of the Path
question: If Muslims must sit in public pathways, what rules must they observe?
notes_sources: The Prophet outlined the rights of the path as: 'Lowering the gaze, refraining from harming, responding to the greetings, ordering the good and eradicating the evil,' as well as 'guiding the one who is lost' [33].

title: The Expiation of the Gathering
question: What should be recited when concluding a sitting or meeting?
notes_sources: It is a Sunnah to expiate for any mistakes or idle talk that occurred by saying: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and to You is the Praise... I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You' (Subhanak Allahumma...). This serves as an expiation for what took place during the sitting [33].

title: The Blessing of the Meal
question: From which part of the plate should a Muslim eat?
notes_sources: The Prophet commanded: 'The blessings descend from the middle of the food. So eat from the edges and do not eat from the middle' [34].

title: Licking the Fingers
question: What should a person do with their fingers after finishing a meal?
notes_sources: The Prophet instructed: 'When one of you eats, he should not wipe his fingers until he licks them or has them licked.' Jabir stated this is because 'You do not know in which part of your food lies its blessing' [34].

title: Patience with Hot Sustenance
question: Why shouldn't a person blow on hot food or into a cup?
notes_sources: A Muslim should not blow over hot food; instead, they must wait until it cools down. Likewise, when drinking water, one should not blow into the glass but rather breathe three times outside of the vessel, separating the glass from the mouth [34, 35].

title: Starting with the Right
question: In what daily matters is it preferred to use the right side?
notes_sources: Aisha noted: 'Allah’s Messenger loved to begin with the right in all his matters, in putting on his shoes, in combing his hair and in purifying himself.' This rule generally applies to all noble and clean tasks [36].

title: Wearing New Clothes
question: What should you say when you see a fellow Muslim wearing new clothes?
notes_sources: It is a Sunnah to pray for them by saying: 'May you wear it until it disintegrates and falls apart' (meaning, may you have a long, blessed life). The Prophet made this supplication when he saw Umm Khalid wearing new clothing [36].

title: The Etiquette of Sleeping
question: What specific words of Dhikr are highly recommended before sleeping?
notes_sources: When Ali and Fatimah asked the Prophet for a servant to help with chores, he taught them something better: 'When you go to your beds, glorify Allah thirty-three times (SubhanAllah), praise Him thirty-three times (Alhamdulillah), and extol His greatness thirty-four times (Allahu Akbar)' [37].

title: The Six Obligations
question: What are the six basic obligations a Muslim owes to another?
notes_sources: 1. Greet them when meeting; 2. Respond when invited; 3. Give sincere advice when sought; 4. Say 'Yarhamukallah' when they sneeze and praise Allah; 5. Visit them when ill; 6. Attend their funeral when they die [8, 38].

title: The Etiquette of Sneezing
question: How should the response (Tashmeet) to a sneeze differ based on who sneezes?
notes_sources: After the sneezer says 'Alhamdulillah', a man should respond ('Yarhamukallah') to an elderly woman in an audible voice, but respond to a young woman in a low voice (audible only to himself). If the sneezer does not say 'Alhamdulillah', no response is required [39].

title: The Forty-Day Limit
question: What is the absolute maximum time allowed for clipping nails and trimming hair?
notes_sources: Anas reported: 'A time limit has been prescribed for us for clipping the moustache and nails, plucking underarm hair and removing pubic hair, that it should not be left for more than forty days.' Spending more than 40 days without doing it is prohibited [40, 41].

title: Burying Removed Body Parts
question: What should be done with clipped nails and removed hair?
notes_sources: It has been commanded in the tradition to appropriately bury four things out of respect for the human body: human blood, hair (from any part of the body), nails, and cloth used for cleaning menstrual blood [42].

title: The Adornment of the Angels
question: What is the virtue of wearing an Imamah, especially on Friday?
notes_sources: The Prophet pointed to the Imamah and said, 'The crowns of angels are like this.' Ibn Umar advised his son to wear it on Fridays because the angels descend wearing Imamahs and send salutations upon those who wear them until the sun sets [43].

title: The Greeting (Salam) Rewards
question: How do the words used in the Salam impact your reward?
notes_sources: Saying 'Assalamu Alaikum' earns 10 virtues. Adding 'Wa Rahmatullah' increases it to 20 virtues. Completing it with 'Wa Barakatuhu' earns 30 virtues. This demonstrates how easily a Muslim can multiply their good deeds in daily interactions [44].

title: Conveying the Salam
question: If someone tells you, 'Give my salam to so-and-so,' how should you respond?
notes_sources: You should not make an immediate reply to the Salam yourself, as your reply is not the objective. Rather, you must faithfully convey the greeting to the intended person. When that person receives it, they should reply: 'Alayka wa Alayhis-Salam' (peace be upon you and him) [45].

title: Innovations in Purity
question: Is it a Sunnah to wipe the neck during ablution (Wudhu)?
notes_sources: No. Wiping the neck during Wudhu is listed among the common mistakes widespread among Muslims. The established Sunnah is to wipe the entire head and the ears, without extending the wiping down to the neck [46].

title: Wiping Over Footwear
question: When wiping over leather socks (Khuff) or regular socks, should the bottom be wiped?
notes_sources: No. Wiping the bottom of the khuff or sock is a common mistake. Islamic law prescribes that only the top of the sock is to be wiped, demonstrating that religion is based on revelation rather than pure human logic [46, 47].

title: Honoring the Prescribed Times
question: What is the consequence of delaying prayer past its appointed window?
notes_sources: Delaying the prayer past its prescribed time without a valid Islamic excuse is a severe mistake. Prayers are enjoined at fixed hours, and consistently missing these windows disrupts the foundational pillar of the religion [48].

title: Words in the Wrong Posture
question: Is it permissible to recite the Quran while bowing (Rukoo') or prostrating (Sujood)?
notes_sources: No. Reciting the Quran during Rukoo' and Sujood is strictly forbidden [49]. These postures are specifically reserved for glorifying Allah and making intense supplications (Du'aa) [50].

title: Guarding the Gaze in Worship
question: Where should a worshipper look during the prayer?
notes_sources: A worshipper must look at the place of prostration. Raising the eyes towards the sky or looking to the right and left without necessity is a major mistake that breaks 'Khushu' (humility/focus) and allows Shaytan to steal from the prayer [50].

title: Distractions of the Hands
question: Why shouldn't a person interlock their fingers during prayer?
notes_sources: Interlocking the fingers, cracking the knuckles, or unnecessarily fidgeting with clothes and watches are all mistakes that distract the person and void the tranquility (Tum'aneenah) required for a valid prayer [51, 52].

title: Modesty in the Mosque
question: What rule must women observe when attending the mosque?
notes_sources: It is a mistake for women to come to the masjid beautified and perfumed. The mosque is a place of worship and humility, and both men and women must observe modesty to prevent distraction and temptation [53].

title: Haste in Supplication
question: What mindset can prevent a supplication from being answered?
notes_sources: A major mistake in Du'aa is losing hope that it will be accepted and being hasty in waiting for a response. A believer must supplicate with certainty and patience, knowing Allah answers in the manner and time He deems best [53].

title: Disrupting the Sermon
question: What action strictly violates the etiquette of the Friday congregation?
