notes_sources: Stepping over the necks of people to get to the front while the Imam is delivering the sermon is a grave error. Once, the Prophet saw a man doing this and commanded him: 'Sit down, for you have annoyed (people)' [54].

title: Ruining the Fast
question: How do visual and auditory sins affect a fasting person?
notes_sources: Fasting is not just abstaining from food. Listening to music or watching romance and detective movies during Ramadan are mistakes that corrupt the ears and eyes, encourage wickedness, and destroy the spiritual reward of the fast [55, 56].

title: Innovations on the Day of Arafah
question: Do pilgrims need to climb Mount Arafah to complete their Hajj?
notes_sources: No. Climbing Mount Arafah as an act of worship, or specifically facing the mountain instead of the Qiblah while supplicating, are common innovations. The entirety of the plain of Arafah is valid for standing [57].

title: Obstacles to Marriage
question: How does an excessively high dowry (Mahr) harm society?
notes_sources: Demanding an excessively high Mahr is a major societal mistake. It creates an artificial barrier to marriage, leading youth to delay it indefinitely (often until after studies), which opens the doors to temptation and corruption in the community [58].

title: Complaining About the Era
question: Why is it forbidden to curse or insult the time/days/years?
notes_sources: The Prophet said: 'Let none of you say, 'O woe is the time,' for surely Allah is the Time.' Because Allah alternates the night and the day, insulting time is effectively directing an insult toward the Creator who decrees what happens within it [59, 60].

title: Barriers to Purity
question: How does wearing nail polish affect Wudhu?
notes_sources: Using modern nail polish creates a waterproof barrier over the nails. Since water must touch all required skin and nails for ablution to be valid, wearing it prevents water from reaching the nail, rendering the Wudhu (and subsequent prayers) invalid [61].

title: The Limits of Grief
question: What is the maximum duration for mourning a deceased person?
notes_sources: It is a mistake to mourn the deceased for more than three days, as this contradicts submission to Allah's decree. The sole exception is a wife mourning the death of her husband, which is prescribed as four months and ten days [62].

title: Dental Hygiene as Worship
question: When is the use of the tooth-stick (Miswak) most highly recommended?
notes_sources: The Miswak purifies the mouth and pleases the Lord. While good at any time, it is heavily emphasized at five times: before prayer, before reading Quran, upon waking from sleep, when the taste of the mouth changes, and when entering the home [63].

title: Changing Grey Hair
question: What is the Islamic ruling on dyeing white or grey hair?
notes_sources: It is highly recommended to change the color of grey hair to differ from the practices of other nations. The best materials to use are henna and 'katm' (yielding a reddish/brownish dye), but dyeing the hair completely black is strictly forbidden [64].

title: The Method of the Call
question: What physical action should the Mu'adhin (caller) take while giving the Adhan?
notes_sources: It is a Sunnah for the caller to insert his index fingers into his ears. This practice stems from Bilal, the Prophet's caller, who said, 'I put my index fingers into my ears and made the adhan.' It is also recommended he turn his head right and left for 'Hayya 'alas-salah' and 'Hayya 'alal-falah' [65, 66].

title: The Ultimate Salutation
question: What is the immense reward for reciting Salawat upon the Prophet?
notes_sources: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) gave the glad tidings: 'Whoever recites Salat upon me once; Allah sends ten mercies upon him, forgives ten sins and elevates his rank by ten times.' It acts as a light on the Day of Judgment [67].

title: The Soul of the Deed
question: How does intention transform everyday actions?
notes_sources: The intention is the soul of the deed. A Muslim bases all deeds on a pious intention, as a permissible act can become an act of obedience worthy of reward simply through a good intention [1]. Conversely, an act of obedience void of pious intention becomes a burden [1].

title: Initiating the Greeting
question: Who should initiate the greeting of peace?
notes_sources: When Muslims meet, the one riding should greet the one walking, the one walking should greet the one sitting, and the smaller group should greet the larger group [2]. It is also recommended to greet both those you know and those you do not know [3].

title: The Etiquette of Handshakes
question: How should Muslims shake hands when meeting?
notes_sources: Shaking hands completes the greeting of Salaam [4]. It is a Sunnah to use both hands for the handshake, and there should not be any cloth or barrier between the palms [5], [6].

title: Seating in a Gathering
question: Where should a person sit when entering a gathering?
notes_sources: A person should sit at the end of the gathering where there is space. They must not make someone else stand up to take their seat [7]. Additionally, the Prophet strictly forbade sitting in the open space in the middle of a circle or gathering [8].

title: Expiation for the Gathering
question: What should be recited when concluding a sitting?
notes_sources: To expiate for any mistakes or idle talk during a gathering, one should seek Allah's forgiveness upon concluding by reciting: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and to You is the Praise. I bear witness that none is worthy of worship except You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You' [9], [10].

title: The Etiquette of Sneezing
question: How should Muslims respond when someone sneezes?
notes_sources: The one who sneezes should praise Allah. It is then an obligation for the listener to audibly say 'Yarhamukallah' (May Allah have mercy on you). The sneezer then replies, 'May Allah guide you and set your affairs aright' [3], [11].

title: The Sunnah of Footwear
question: In what order should shoes be put on and removed?
notes_sources: When putting on shoes, a Muslim must begin with the right foot, and when taking them off, they must begin with the left foot [12], [13]. It is also prohibited to walk wearing only one shoe; one should either wear both or walk barefoot [12].

title: The Natural Disposition
question: What are the five acts of the natural disposition?
notes_sources: Five acts are part of the Fitrah: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, plucking armpit hairs, cutting the nails, and trimming the mustache [14]. The Prophet set a time limit that these should not be left for more than forty days [15].

title: The Application of Fragrance
question: What are the guidelines for using fragrance for men and women?
notes_sources: The Prophet stated that the fragrance for men is one whose smell is apparent but its color is hidden, while the fragrance for women is one whose color is visible but its smell is hidden [16]. Women are prohibited from wearing perfume when going to the mosque or leaving the house if unrelated men can smell it [17].

title: The Virtue of Lending
question: What is the spiritual reward for giving a loan to someone in need?
notes_sources: The Prophet stated that every loan is an act of charity (Sadaqah) [18]. Easing the burden of a debtor is highly rewarded; helping those in difficulties strengthens social cohesion and love within the community [19].

title: The Sin of Scoffing
question: Why is mocking or scoffing at others strictly forbidden?
notes_sources: Allah explicitly forbids groups of men or women from scoffing at one another, noting that the mocked person may be better in the sight of Allah than the mocker [20], [21]. It is also forbidden to insult one another with offensive nicknames [22].

title: Avoiding Suspicion
question: Why must believers avoid undue suspicion?
notes_sources: The Prophet warned to avoid suspicion because it is the 'falsest of speech' [23]. Suspicion leads to spying on others and seeking out their private faults, which destroys brotherhood and breeds animosity [20], [24].

title: The Past is Gone
question: Why should a Muslim avoid brooding over past tragedies?
notes_sources: Brooding over the past is a sickness that destroys your resolve for the present moment. Episodes of the past are finished, and sadness cannot retrieve them; a believer should not 'carry out an autopsy' on history but instead focus on today [25].

title: Casting Off Anxiety
question: How does trusting in predestination cure anxiety?
notes_sources: Do not be sad over what has been preordained, as it will take place regardless. The pens have dried, and the scrolls have been rolled up [26]. Recognizing that Allah forgets sins and accepts repentance brings peace to the heart and drives away worry [26].

title: Handling Criticism
question: How should you respond to jealousy and unjust criticism?
notes_sources: Accept constructive criticism, but realize that the jealous and weak-minded will always exist [27]. The more you achieve, the more you may face envy, so do not broadcast all your affairs to sitting companions who might rejoice at your misfortune [28].

title: Distractions in the Mosque
question: Why is it forbidden to interlock fingers while waiting for prayer?
notes_sources: Interlacing the fingers or cracking the knuckles in the mosque is a distraction from Shaytan [29], [30]. A person is considered to be in a state of prayer from the moment they perform Wudhu and head to the mosque, so they must maintain tranquility [31].

title: The Sanctity of the Praying Person
question: What is the sin of walking directly in front of someone praying?
notes_sources: The Prophet said that if a person knew the burden of sin they bear by passing in front of a praying person (between them and their Sutrah), they would prefer to stand and wait for 40 years rather than pass [32], [33].

title: The Seven Bones of Prostration
question: Which body parts must firmly touch the ground during prostration?
notes_sources: The Prophet was ordered to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead (including the nose), the two hands (palms), the two knees, and the toes of both feet [34], [35]. Raising the feet off the ground invalidates the prostration [36].

title: Tranquility in Action
question: Why is rushing through the prayer so dangerous?
notes_sources: The absence of ease and tranquility invalidates the prayer entirely [37]. A worshipper must bow and prostrate until every bone and joint settles at ease; the Prophet commanded a man who prayed hastily to repeat his prayer because 'he had not prayed' [38], [39].

title: Following the Imam
question: What happens if a person purposely bows or prostrates before the Imam?
notes_sources: Preceding the Imam in the prayer purposely invalidates that rak'ah or the entire prayer [37], [40]. The Imam is appointed to be followed; worshippers must not say the takbeer or move into the next pillar until the Imam has done so first [41].

title: The Extraction of the Soul
question: How does the soul leave the body at death?
notes_sources: For a believer, the angel of death gently tells the soul to come out to Allah's forgiveness, and it flows out smoothly like a drop from a waterskin [42]. For a disbeliever, the angel extracts it harshly, and it is given to angels of punishment [43], [44].

title: The Trial of the Grave
question: What three questions are asked by Munkar and Nakir in the grave?
notes_sources: Two angels will make the deceased sit up and ask: 'Who is your Lord?', 'What is your deen?', and 'Who is this man sent among you?' The believer answers correctly, while the disbeliever stammers 'Alas, I do not know' [45], [46].

title: Washing the Deceased
question: What are the rules for washing a deceased Muslim?
notes_sources: Washing the body is a communal obligation (Fard Kifaayah) [47]. Men wash men, and women wash women, using water and sidr (lote-tree leaves), washing it an odd number of times (three, five, or seven) [48]. Spouses may wash each other [47].

title: Shrouding the Deceased
question: How should a deceased Muslim be shrouded?
notes_sources: It is a Sunnah to shroud a male in three white cotton cloths that are rolled up around the body without a shirt or turban [49], [50]. A female is typically shrouded in five pieces of cloth, including a veil and wrap [49].

title: The Funeral Prayer Mechanics
question: What is recited during the funeral prayer?
notes_sources: The prayer consists of four Takbeers. After the first, Al-Fatihah is recited. After the second, Salawat upon the Prophet. After the third, sincere supplication for the deceased. After the fourth, a Tasleem is given to conclude [51], [52].

title: The Funeral Procession
question: What is the proper etiquette when following a funeral bier?
notes_sources: Following the funeral is a right a Muslim owes another [53]. Participants should hasten with the procession without running, and it is strictly forbidden to raise voices in loud weeping, chanting, or engaging in un-Islamic customs [54], [55].

title: Placing the Body in the Grave
question: How must the body be positioned inside the grave?
notes_sources: The body should be entered from the foot of the grave and placed on its right side facing the Qiblah. The person placing the body should say: 'Bismillahi wa 'alaa sunnati rasoolillah' (With the name of Allah and upon the Sunnah of Allah's Messenger) [56], [57].

title: The Limits of Mourning
question: How long is a Muslim permitted to mourn a death?
notes_sources: It is forbidden for a woman to mourn any deceased person for more than three days, except for her husband, whom she mourns for four months and ten days [58]. During this specific period (Iddah), the widow must not wear adornments, perfume, or jewelry [59], [58].

title: Visiting the Graveyard
question: What is the Islamic purpose of visiting graves?
notes_sources: Visiting graves is prescribed to remind oneself of the Hereafter and to supplicate for the deceased [60], [61]. It is strictly forbidden to call upon the dead in supplication, seek their aid, or sit upon the graves [61].

title: Benefiting the Dead
question: What actions of the living can benefit a person after they die?
notes_sources: The deceased benefits from the sincere supplications of Muslims, the payment of their outstanding debts, righteous children praying for them, and any continuing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah) or beneficial knowledge they left behind [62], [61].

title: The Trumpet Blast
question: What happens when the Trumpet is blown?
notes_sources: The Trumpet will be blown, causing all in the heavens and earth to lose consciousness and die. When it is blown a second time, everyone will instantly stand upright from their graves, resurrected and looking on in horror [63], [64].

title: The Resurrection
question: What is the physical state of humans when resurrected?
notes_sources: Mankind will be raised up barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, just as they were originally created [65], [66]. The whole human body wastes away in the earth except for the coccyx bone, from which Allah recreates the body [64].

title: The Gathering
question: How will people be herded to the place of Judgment?
notes_sources: The believers will be gathered with ceremony, riding toward the Mercy of Allah [67]. Conversely, the evildoers and disbelievers will be gathered flat on their faces—blind, dumb, and deaf—driven toward Hell [68], [67].

title: Drenched in Sweat
question: What physical trial will mankind face while waiting for judgment?
notes_sources: The sun will be brought so close to creation that people will be drenched in their own sweat. Depending on their worldly deeds, sweat will reach their knees, their waists, or even bridle their mouths [69].

title: The Five Ultimate Questions
question: What must every person answer for before moving on the Day of Judgment?
notes_sources: The Prophet stated that no one's feet will move until they are questioned about five things: how they spent their life, what they did with their youth, how they earned their wealth, how they spent it, and how they acted upon their knowledge [70], [71].

title: The Scales of Justice
question: What exactly will be weighed on the Day of Judgment?
notes_sources: Allah will set up the Balances of Justice. The texts indicate that the actual deeds (taking physical forms), the records and scrolls of those deeds, and even the physical weight of the slave themselves will all be weighed [72], [73].

title: Crossing the Bridge
question: How is the Bridge over Hell described?
notes_sources: The Sirat is laid over the Fire of Hell; it is slippery, lined with massive hooks and thorns [72], [74]. Believers will cross it at different speeds—like lightning, wind, or swift horses—while others will be snatched and fall into the Fire [74].

title: The Great Intercession
question: Who will intercede to begin the Judgment?
notes_sources: Prophet Muhammad will be granted the Great Intercession. He will fall prostrate beneath the Throne until Allah grants him permission to speak and intercede [75], [76]. Later, angels, prophets, and martyrs will also be permitted to intercede [76].

title: The Slaughter of Death
question: Will anyone ever die in Paradise or Hell?
notes_sources: No. Death will be brought forth in the visual form of a beautiful sheep and slaughtered on the barrier between Paradise and Hell. A caller will then announce to both groups that there is only eternity and no more death [77], [78].

title: Entering the Abode of Bliss
question: What happens at the gates of Paradise?
notes_sources: Believers will be welcomed by angels saying 'Peace be upon you.' Those who dedicated themselves to specific worship will be called from specific gates, such as the Gate of Prayer, the Gate of Charity, or Bab Ar-Rayyan for those who fasted [79], [80].

title: Levels of Paradise
question: Are there different ranks within Paradise?
notes_sources: Yes, Paradise has one hundred grades or levels. If the entire world gathered in just one of them, it would be sufficient [81]. A person reading the Quran is told to read and ascend, climbing a degree for every verse [81].

title: The Lowest Rank in Jannah
question: What does the last person to enter Paradise receive?
notes_sources: The very last man to exit Hell and enter Paradise will be granted by Allah the equivalent of the greatest kingdom of the world, and then ten times more like it, along with whatever his heart desires [82], [83].

title: The Highest Rank (Al-Wasilah)
question: What is the ultimate station in Paradise?
notes_sources: Al-Wasilah is the absolute highest rank, positioned above all other ranks, reserved for only one chosen servant of Allah—Prophet Muhammad. Believers are encouraged to pray for him to attain it after every Adhan [84], [85].

title: The Garments of the Believers
question: What will the inhabitants of Paradise wear?
notes_sources: They will be adorned with bracelets of gold and silver, garlands of pearls, and green garments of fine silk and rich brocade [86], [87]. Their garments will never wear out, and their youth will never fade [88].

title: The Ornaments and Crowns
question: How beautiful will the adornments of Jannah be?
notes_sources: Believers will wear crowns like kings [89]. If a man from Paradise were to look down and his bracelet appeared, its brilliance would blot out the light of the sun just as the sun blots out the stars [90].

title: Couches and Thrones
question: Where will the believers recline?
notes_sources: They will recline facing each other on couches (Ara'ik) raised high, woven with gold fabrics and studded with pearls, rubies, and chrysolite [91], [92]. These beds will have curtained canopies prepared for total relaxation [92].

title: The Maidens of Paradise
question: Who are the Hoor Al-'Ayn?
notes_sources: They are beautiful, dark-eyed maidens of Paradise, created in perfection [93]. They are immortal, fresh, and will never fade, welcoming the believers to their eternal homes with joy and sweet singing [94], [95].

title: The Markets of Jannah
question: What happens in the markets of Paradise?
notes_sources: Believers will visit a market surrounded by angels, containing things no eye has seen. They can take whatever they wish without buying or selling [96]. Upon returning to their spouses, their beauty and radiance will have increased significantly [97].

title: The Day of More
question: What special event occurs every Friday in Paradise?
notes_sources: Friday is the 'Day of More.' The inhabitants will gather in a vast valley of white musk on pulpits of light, gold, and gems [98], [99]. Allah will shower them with fragrances and grant them bounties beyond imagination [100].

title: The Ultimate Delight
question: What is the greatest reward in Paradise?
notes_sources: The absolute greatest delight is gazing upon the Face of Allah [101]. The believers will see Him as clearly as one sees the full moon, and Allah will speak to them directly, a joy that surpasses all physical pleasures [102], [103].

title: Earning a Lawful Livelihood
question: Why is earning Halal wealth so crucial?
notes_sources: Any flesh nourished by unlawful wealth is more entitled to the Fire [104], [105]. If a person earns unlawful money, even their prayers and acts of charity with that wealth are rejected by Allah [104], [106].

title: Speculative Transactions (Gharar)
question: Why are overly risky sales forbidden?
notes_sources: Selling something with an overwhelming presence of undue risk or uncertainty (Gharar) is forbidden because it is tantamount to gambling and unjustly devouring another's wealth [107], [108].

title: The Crime of Usury (Riba)
question: How severe is the sin of interest?
notes_sources: Riba is a heinous crime that destroys society by feeding greed without effort [109], [110]. The Prophet cursed the one who takes interest, the one who pays it, the one who records it, and the two witnesses, stating they are all alike in sin [111].

title: The Evil of Hoarding
question: What is the punishment for hoarding essential goods?
notes_sources: A merchant who hoards staple foods to artificially inflate prices is cursed [112]. The Prophet warned that anyone who hoards grain for forty days has washed his hands of Allah, and Allah has washed His hands of him [113], [114].

title: Fraud and Deception
question: Can you conceal a defect in a product you are selling?
notes_sources: No. The Prophet said, 'Whoever deceives us is not from us' [115]. It is obligatory to point out any faults in the merchandise. Intentionally concealing a defect destroys the blessing of the entire transaction [73], [116].

title: Selling What You Do Not Own
question: Can you sell an item before you actually possess it?
notes_sources: It is prohibited to sell goods that you do not physically possess or own [117], [118]. This ensures trade remains fair and prevents disputes over items that the seller cannot guarantee they can procure.

title: Two Transactions in One
question: What is an 'Eenah transaction?
notes_sources: It involves selling an item for a deferred higher price, and then immediately buying it back from the buyer for a lower cash price [119]. This is a prohibited trick to execute a loan with interest under the guise of a sale [119].

title: Undercutting a Brother's Sale
question: Can you outbid another Muslim's established sale?
notes_sources: The Prophet said, 'No man should sell over the sale of his brother' [120]. Offering a buyer a lower price after they have already agreed to a purchase with someone else breeds hatred, envy, and boycotting [121].

title: Artificially Inflating Prices (Najsh)
question: What is Najsh in business?
notes_sources: Najsh is when a person offers the seller more than the selling price without any intention of buying it, simply to deceive the actual buyer into paying more [122], [121]. The Prophet strictly forbade this deceitful practice [122].

title: Trading in the Impermissible
question: Is it allowed to sell Haram items if you do not consume them yourself?
notes_sources: No. Selling alcohol, indecent magazines, or anything Allah has forbidden is prohibited. The rule is: 'When Allah forbids a thing, He also forbids its price' [123], [124]. The money earned from it is unlawful.

title: The Obligation of Justice
question: To whom must a Muslim be just?
notes_sources: A Muslim must be just to everyone—rich and poor, friend and foe, Muslim and non-Muslim, and even to their own soul [125]. Allah commands believers to stand firmly for justice, even if it goes against themselves or their parents [126], [127].

title: Ordering Good and Forbidding Evil
question: What happens if Muslims abandon forbidding evil?
notes_sources: Enjoining good and forbidding evil is an essential part of faith [128]. If a society abandons this duty, they risk being deprived of good, facing Allah's punishment, and having their supplications rejected [129], [128].

title: Mutual Support
question: How should believers support one another?
notes_sources: Believers are like a single building, reinforcing one another [130], [131]. If a Muslim brother is being oppressed, one must come to his aid. The Prophet commanded: 'Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or he is oppressed' (helping the oppressor means stopping his oppression) [132], [133].

title: Repelling Evil with Goodness
question: How should you deal with antagonism from others?
notes_sources: Allah commands believers to repel evil with a deed that is better. By doing so, the one between whom you had enmity may become as though he was a close friend [113].

title: Dealing with Non-Muslims
question: How should a Muslim treat non-belligerent non-Muslims?
notes_sources: With justice, equity, and good behavior. A Muslim must fulfill trusts to them, must not deceive them, and may not wrong them with respect to their life, wealth, or honor [134], [135], [136].

title: Kindness Towards Animals
question: Does Islam dictate how we treat animals?
notes_sources: Yes. It is prohibited to harm an animal without just cause. A Muslim earns divine reward for feeding or giving water to a hungry or thirsty animal [137]. The Prophet cursed anyone who uses a living creature as an archery target [138].

title: Gratitude to Parents
question: Why does Islam place such high emphasis on parents?
notes_sources: Allah closely ties the command to worship Him alone with good behavior toward parents [139]. The mother, in particular, has the greatest right to excellent companionship, surpassing even the father, due to her sacrifices [140], [141].

title: Equitability Among Children
question: Can a parent give a special financial gift to only one child?
notes_sources: No. Islam prohibits showing favoritism among children, as it corrupts their souls with envy and destroys family cohesion. The Prophet ordered a father who gave a slave to only one son to take it back, saying, 'I will not be a witness to an injustice' [142], [143].

title: The Rights of Close Relatives
question: How should one treat extended family?
notes_sources: One must treat aunts and uncles like parents, respecting elders and showing mercy to the young [144]. Giving charity to a poor relative yields a double reward: one for charity and one for upholding ties of kinship [145].

title: Maintaining Ties of Kinship
question: What is the consequence of severing family ties?
notes_sources: Maintaining ties of kinship results in reward, increased provisions, and a prolonged lifespan [146]. Severing ties is a major sin; the Prophet stated that the person who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise [147].

title: Mutual Rights of Spouses
question: What is the core foundation of interactions between husband and wife?
notes_sources: The overarching rule is to 'live with them honorably' [148], [149]. There must be mutual trust, love, mercy, and sincerity. A husband must be fair and just, while the wife obeys him in matters that do not disobey Allah [150], [151].

title: Guarding Marital Secrets
question: What is the ruling on discussing intimate marital details with others?
notes_sources: It is strictly forbidden. The Prophet warned that the people in the worst position in Allah's sight on the Day of Resurrection are those who spread the intimate secrets of their spouses to others [152], [153].

title: Moderation in Spending
question: What is the Islamic stance on family expenditure?
notes_sources: A Muslim must spend on his dependents without meanness or extravagance [154]. Squandering wealth makes one a 'brother to the devils,' while being stingy exposes the family to social decay. Balance is the key [154].

title: Extravagance in Weddings
question: Why does Islam warn against excessively high dowries (Mahr)?
notes_sources: An outrageously high dowry creates artificial barriers to marriage, leading youth to delay it and opening doors to temptation [155], [156]. Likewise, going to excess regarding wedding food and lights violates the command against extravagance [157].

title: Blurring Gender Distinctions
question: Is it permissible for men and women to wear each other's styles?
notes_sources: It is strictly prohibited. The Prophet cursed men who imitate women and women who imitate men in their clothing, appearance, or mannerisms [158]. Each gender has clothing specific to them to maintain distinct modesty [158].

title: Garments of Fame
question: What is a 'garment of fame' (Libas al-Shuhrah)?
notes_sources: These are excessively extravagant or deliberately unusual clothes worn specifically to draw attention and become famous among people. The Prophet warned that whoever wears a garment of fame, Allah will dress him in a garment of humiliation [159], [160].

title: The Dress of Ihram for Women
question: Do women have a specific Ihram garment like men do?
notes_sources: No. Women do not have specific unstitched garments for Ihram. They may wear their regular permissible clothes, with the sole exception that they must not wear face veils (Niqab) or gloves while in the state of Ihram [161], [162].

title: Praying at the Prophet's Mosque
question: Is it obligatory to visit the Prophet's grave for Hajj to be valid?
notes_sources: No. Believing Hajj is incomplete without visiting the Prophet's grave is a mistake [163]. However, it is highly recommended to travel to pray in the Prophet's Mosque due to its virtue, and while there, one respectfully conveys salaam to the Prophet without lingering excessively [164].

title: Protecting Deeds from Riyaa'
question: What happens if an act of worship is done for showing off?
notes_sources: If a deed is performed to seek the praise of people alongside Allah, Allah rejects it entirely [165], [166]. Sincerity means the deed is completely free from showing off (Riyaa'), which is considered minor shirk [166].

title: Obedience to Leaders
question: When is a Muslim obligated to obey leaders?
notes_sources: Muslims must obey their leaders and abide by the laws of the state, provided those laws do not command disobedience to Allah [167], [168]. If ordered to commit a sin, there is no obedience to the creation in disobedience to the Creator [169].

title: The Five Phases of Mortality
question: What are the five distinct stages of human life?
notes_sources: According to scholars, human life is divided into five phases: childhood (birth to puberty), youthfulness (puberty to 35), maturity (35 to 50), old age (50 to 70), and decrepitude (70 until death).

title: The Season of Youth
question: What characterizes the stage of youth?
notes_sources: Spanning from puberty until 35 years of age, this is the peak of physical strength and desire. A believer must fiercely struggle against their desires during this stage, as protecting the self in youth yields immense spiritual reward.

title: The Dawn of Maturity
question: What happens during the stage of maturity?
notes_sources: From age 35 to 50, physical youthfulness begins to wane, and the 'grey hair arrives with its soldiers.' It is a critical period demanding serious reflection and repentance, as the nearness of mortality becomes undeniable.

title: The Stage of Old Age
question: How should a believer approach old age?
notes_sources: From 50 to 70, physical desires weaken significantly. Therefore, if an old person commits a sin purposefully, it is spiritually worse because the driving lust has extinguished. The Prophet severely warned against an old person who commits adultery.

title: Conveying the Prophetic Words
question: What is the reward for preserving and transmitting Islamic knowledge?
notes_sources: The Prophet stated: 'If any person memorizes 40 Ahadees pertaining to Islamic matters for conveying them to my Ummah, Allah will resurrect him as an Islamic scholar on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be an Intercessor and a witness for him.'

title: The Angel at the Grave
question: How does the Prophet know when someone sends blessings upon him?
notes_sources: Allah has appointed an angel to the Prophet's grave with the ability to hear all creation. Whenever someone recites Salat upon the Prophet, the angel presents the person's name and father's name directly to him.

title: Light on the Sirat
question: How does sending blessings upon the Prophet help on Judgment Day?
notes_sources: Recitation of Salat upon the Prophet serves as Noor (light) on the highly treacherous bridge of Siraat. Whoever recites it 80 times on Friday, their sins of 80 years will be forgiven.

title: The Ultimate Level of Worship
question: What is the highest tier of faith in Islam?
notes_sources: Ihsaan is to worship Allah as if you see Him in front of you. Even though you do not physically see Him, you worship with the absolute certainty that He sees you. It demands a state of constant awareness and complete sincerity.

title: The Finality of the Message
question: Why can there be no prophets after Muhammad?
notes_sources: He was sent for all of humankind until the Day of Judgment, superseding and canceling the remnants of all previous teachings. Anyone claiming prophethood after him is considered a liar, and accepting them negates one's Islam entirely.

title: Physical Compliance
question: Does faith only exist in the heart?
notes_sources: No. True faith requires submission and compliance, meaning the actual physical enactment of deeds. The very word 'Islam' means submission to the will and commands of Allah through physical action.

title: The Components of True Repentance
question: What three conditions must be met for repentance to be valid?
notes_sources: 1. Stopping the sin immediately. 2. Feeling deep remorse for committing it. 3. Having a sincere, firm intention never to return to the sin again. Without these three components, repentance is incomplete.

title: The Test of Quality
question: Does Allah judge us by the quantity or quality of our deeds?
notes_sources: Allah created life and death to test who is 'best in deed' (Quran 67:1-2). He did not create us to perform the most deeds with the least quality; He seeks pure intentions and correct execution according to the Sunnah.

title: The Dimensions of the Kursee
question: How vast is Allah's Footstool (Kursee)?
notes_sources: Ayat al-Kursee affirms that Allah's Kursee extends over and completely fits all of the heavens and the earth. It is a real, immense creation that demonstrates the unfathomable majesty and greatness of the Creator.

title: The Greatest Creation
question: What is the largest creation of Allah?
notes_sources: The Throne (Arsh) is the greatest of all creations. The Prophet compared the seven heavens to a mere ring thrown in a vast desert compared to the Kursee, and the Kursee to the Arsh is like that ring in the desert.

title: The Absolute Highness
question: Where is Allah in relation to His creation?
notes_sources: Allah is the Most High. He is above the heavens and above the Throne, completely separate from and above His creation. His highness is real and literal, not merely a symbolic highness of status.

title: The Divine Voice
question: Will Allah speak directly to humanity?
notes_sources: Allah has a Voice that is perfect, majestic, and completely unlike the voices of creation. On Judgment Day, He will call out with a Voice heard equally by those far away and those near, speaking directly to each person without a translator.

title: The Eternal Life
question: How does Allah's Life differ from creation?
notes_sources: Allah's life is eternal and perfect, extending from before creation without a beginning, and it never ends. He is Al-Hayy (The Ever-Living) who sustains all things and is never overtaken by slumber or sleep.

title: The Unfathomable Knowledge
question: What is the extent of Allah's knowledge?
notes_sources: With Him are the keys of the unseen. Not a single leaf falls from a tree, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth, except that He knows it perfectly and it is written in a clear record.

title: Erasing the Weight of Sins
question: What specific phrase multiplies praise immensely?
notes_sources: Reciting 'Subhaanallaahi wa Bihamdihi' 100 times equates to 124,000 good deeds. However, one must beware of letting the bounties of this world consume those deeds through lack of gratitude or committing sins.

title: The Meaning of the Praises
question: How did Ali ibn Abi Talib explain 'Subhaanallah' and 'Alhamdulillah'?
notes_sources: 'Alhamdulillah' is a phrase Allah is pleased to have His servants use, while 'Subhaanallah' means expressing Allaah's absolute purity from any defect, flaw, or anything unsuitable for His Majesty.

title: Seeking Refuge from Internal Evils
question: What specific internal weaknesses did the Prophet seek refuge from?
notes_sources: The Prophet regularly sought refuge in Allah from four destructive matters: knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that does not submit/fear Allah, a soul that is never satiated, and a supplication that is not answered.

title: The Pebbles of Tasbeeh
question: How did inanimate objects recognize the Prophet?
notes_sources: While sitting with Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, the Prophet picked up pebbles that audibly engaged in Tasbeeh (glorifying Allah), sounding like the humming of bees. This miraculously continued when placed in the hands of the three Caliphs.

title: The Subservience of the Ocean
question: Did the Sahabah ever experience miracles over nature?
notes_sources: Yes, through immense faith. For instance, the ocean was subjugated for Alaa bin Hadhrami and his army, and the Tigris River miraculously became traversable for the Muslims during the conquest of Madaa'in.

title: The Fire Obeys the Believer
question: How did Tameem Daari interact with a massive fire?
notes_sources: Unseen assistance manifested when a massive fire broke out. Tameem Daari drove the fire away, actively forcing it back into its source while it obeyed him, displaying the authority Allah grants His pious servants over creation.

title: The Heavenly Tree
question: What did the Prophet say about the shade of the trees in Paradise?
notes_sources: A Bedouin asked the Prophet about a tree in Jannah. The Prophet explained that a rider could travel under its shade for a hundred years without reaching its end, highlighting the unimaginable scale of the Hereafter.

title: Leading Unqualified
question: Who should lead the congregational prayer?
notes_sources: It is a major mistake to push forward someone to lead the prayer who is unqualified (lacking Quranic memorization or Fiqh knowledge) while more qualified, knowledgeable people are present in the congregation.

title: Linguistic Errors in Recitation
question: Why is proper pronunciation crucial in Al-Fatihah?
notes_sources: Grammatical mistakes in reciting the Quran, such as changing vowel sounds (like saying 'an'amtu' instead of 'an'amta'), can drastically alter the meaning of the verses and potentially invalidate the prayer entirely.

title: The Impermissibility of Images
question: Why are photographs and statues of living beings forbidden?
notes_sources: Photographing, drawing, or hanging pictures of creatures with souls (humans and animals) in sitting rooms without vital necessity is prohibited, as it imitates the creation of Allah and prevents angels of mercy from entering the home.

title: Maintaining Distinct Identity
question: How do men often unlawfully imitate non-Muslims in grooming?
notes_sources: Shaving the beard and growing the mustache long is a direct imitation of non-Muslims and contradicts the explicit command of the Prophet to 'trim the mustache and leave the beard to grow.'

title: Deception in Appearances
question: Is wearing a wig permissible in Islam?
notes_sources: No. Wearing wigs or hairpieces is strictly prohibited for both men and women, as it is classified under forbidden hair extensions. The Prophet cursed the one who adds hair extensions and the one who has it done.

title: Ignoring Financial Obligations to Kin
question: What is a severe error regarding wealthy individuals and their poor relatives?
notes_sources: Apathy towards spending on relatives whom it is legally or morally mandatory to support is a major sin. Neglecting poor family members while giving to distant charities violates the strict priorities of Islamic financial responsibility.

title: The Perils of Vacationing
question: What are the spiritual dangers of traveling to non-Muslim lands for leisure?
notes_sources: Traveling abroad purely for vacation often leads to neglecting religious obligations, engaging in the impermissible, and failing to give Da'wah or display the beauty of Islam, thereby compromising one's faith.

title: Selling the Unknown
question: Can you sell a product without specifying its details?
notes_sources: Selling an unknown product, or selling a product without clarifying a known defect to the buyer, is heavily prohibited (Gharar). Transparency and honesty are mandatory for a transaction to be valid and blessed.

title: Trading in the Impermissible
question: Is it lawful to sell music or indecent material?
notes_sources: Selling music cassettes, videos featuring immodest images, or media promoting corrupt ideologies is entirely Haram. When Allah forbids a thing, He also forbids its price; thus, the wealth earned is unlawful.

title: Digging a Grave Prematurely
question: Is it a good practice to dig one's own grave before dying?
notes_sources: Digging a grave before death is an innovation (Bid'ah) not practiced by the Prophet or his Companions. Preparing for death should be done through righteous deeds and repentance, not by preemptively digging holes.

title: The Islamic Will (Wasiyyah)
question: What should be the core message of a Muslim's final will?
notes_sources: An Islamic will must testify to the Oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the finality of Muhammad. It should enjoin the family to fear Allah, maintain family ties, and explicitly demand burial according to the Sunnah without innovation.

title: The Sin of Altering a Will
question: What is the consequence of changing someone's will?
notes_sources: If anyone alters a bequest after hearing it, the sin falls entirely upon the one who made the change. Allah strictly warns that He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing regarding the execution of final trusts.

title: Innovations at the Graveyard
question: Is it permissible to recite Surah Yaa-Seen over graves?
notes_sources: Reciting Surah Al-Faatihah or Yaa-Seen specifically over graves is an innovated practice not found in the Sunnah. Visitors should instead use the authentic Prophetic supplications designated for the deceased.

title: Psychological Ruin
question: How do violent video games affect the Muslim mind?
notes_sources: Engaging in violent games exposes sensitive minds to cruelty, desensitizes them to bloodshed, and wastes immense amounts of precious time. This addiction destroys focus on the Hereafter and worldly productivity.

title: The Supplication of the Journey
question: What should a Muslim recite when boarding transportation?
notes_sources: One should say 'Bismillah,' then 'Alhamdulillah,' and recite the verse: 'Glory be to Him Who has given this transportation in our control, and this was not to be in our control. And indeed, we have to return to our Lord.'

title: Seeking Protection on the Road
question: Which Surahs protect a traveler from hardship?
notes_sources: The Prophet advised reciting five Surahs when traveling: Al-Kafiroon, Al-Nasr, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Naas. Each should begin with Bismillah, ensuring immense prosperity and safety throughout the trip.

title: Hastening Back Home
question: Should a Muslim prolong a journey unnecessarily?
notes_sources: No. The Prophet described travel as a 'portion of torment' that keeps a person from normal sleep, drink, and food. Once the objective is achieved, a traveler should return quickly to their family.

title: The Return Supplication
question: What should be said upon returning from a journey?
notes_sources: Upon approaching one's town or home, it is a Sunnah to say 'Allahu Akbar' three times and then state: 'We are returning, repenting, serving our Lord, and praising Him.'

title: The Corruption of the Heart
question: What forms of entertainment destroy Islamic character?
notes_sources: Wasting time on romance movies, detective plays, wrestling, and music corrupts the eyes and ears. These media forms grow wickedness in the heart, encourage sin, and slowly destroy the desire for righteousness.

title: The Supplication of Qunoot
question: What is the traditional du'aa recited during Witr?
notes_sources: The Prophet taught his grandson Al-Hasan to say: 'O Allah, guide me among those whom You have guided, pardon me among those whom You have pardoned, bless me in what You have bestowed, and save me from the evil of what You have decreed.'

title: The Covenant of the Souls
question: When did humanity first testify to Allah's Lordship?
notes_sources: Before birth, Allah brought forth the seed of Adam from their loins and made them testify, asking: 'Am I not your Lord?' They all replied, 'Yes! We testify.' This was done so that no one could claim ignorance on the Day of Resurrection or blame their forefathers for their misguidance.

title: The Four Decrees in the Womb
question: What is written for a fetus while it is still in the mother's womb?
notes_sources: After 120 days of development, an angel is sent to breathe the soul into the fetus. The angel is commanded to write four absolute decrees: its provision, its lifespan, its deeds, and whether it will be doomed or blessed in the Hereafter.

title: The Danger of Fortunetellers
question: What is the Islamic ruling on visiting soothsayers and believing them?
notes_sources: Claiming knowledge of the unseen or believing in soothsayers, fortunetellers, and magicians is an act of disbelief and major Shirk. Allah states clearly in the Quran that 'None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.'

title: The Perfection of Wudhu
question: What is the Prophetic Sunnah for washing the hands and mouth during ablution?
notes_sources: It is highly recommended to wash the hands three times at the very beginning of Wudhu. Furthermore, one should rinse the mouth and sniff water into the nostrils three times, using the right hand to draw the water in and the left hand to blow it out.

title: Wasting Water in Ablution
question: Is it permissible to use excessive amounts of water for Wudhu?
notes_sources: Extravagance and waste are prohibited. Using water beyond the Prophetic example—such as washing body parts more than three times—is considered a transgression and an innovation, even if one is performing Wudhu at a flowing river.

title: Supplications During Wudhu
question: Are there specific prayers to say while washing each individual body part?
notes_sources: There is no authentic hadith stating that specific supplications should be recited while washing specific limbs. The established Sunnah is simply to say 'Bismillah' at the beginning and the Shahadah upon completion.

title: Awaiting the Prayer
question: What physical action should be avoided when walking to the mosque?
notes_sources: Interlocking the fingers is prohibited after one has performed Wudhu at home and is heading to the masjid. The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that the person is legally considered to be in a 'state of prayer' until they return home.

title: Straightening the Back in Bowing
question: How should the back be positioned during Rukoo'?
notes_sources: The worshipper should spread his back and make it completely level, to the point that if water were poured on it, it would stay there and not run off. The head should neither be raised nor lowered, but kept perfectly level with the back.

title: Imitating Animals in Prayer
question: What animal postures are strictly forbidden during Salah?
notes_sources: The Prophet strictly forbade pecking like a rooster (rushing through prostrations), squatting like a dog (resting the buttocks on the ground with knees up), looking around like a fox, and dropping to prostration front-first like a kneeling camel.

title: Prompting the Imam
question: What should a follower do if the Imam hesitates or forgets an Ayah?
notes_sources: It is prescribed and encouraged for the one praying behind the Imam to prompt him and correct his recitation if he forgets a portion of the Quran or hesitates during the prayer.

title: Sitting on the Heels (Iq'aa)
question: Is it ever permissible to rest upon the heels during prayer?
notes_sources: Yes, it is permissible occasionally to sit in Iq'aa—which means resting the buttocks on the heels and the balls of the feet. However, this is specifically prescribed only for the brief sitting between the two prostrations.

title: Pointing the Index Finger
question: How should the right hand be positioned during the Tashahhud sitting?
notes_sources: One should clench the fingers of the right hand, occasionally making a circle with the thumb and middle finger. The index finger should be pointed towards the Qiblah and moved, making du'aa with it from the beginning of the Tashahhud until the end.

title: Qunoot During Calamities
question: When is the Qunoot supplication recited outside of Witr prayer?
notes_sources: It is a Sunnah to recite Qunoot (supplicating aloud after standing up from Rukoo' in the last Rak'ah of obligatory prayers) to pray for the Muslims when a major disaster, calamity, or tragedy befalls the Ummah.

title: Giving Just Weight and Measure
question: What is the Islamic warning against stinting in business?
notes_sources: Giving short weight or measure is severely condemned as a hidden form of theft. Allah promises a terrible woe to those who demand full measure for themselves but hand over less when weighing for others, forgetting they will soon stand before the Lord of the worlds.

title: The Interspace
question: What happens to a person who dies desiring to return to the world to do good?
notes_sources: When death comes to a transgressor, they beg to be sent back to act rightly. The Quran declares, 'No indeed! It is just words he utters.' Before them is an interspace (Barzakh) until the Day they are raised, sealing their earthly deeds forever.

title: The Testifying of the Skin
question: How will a person's own body bear witness against them?
notes_sources: On the Day of Reckoning, mouths will be sealed, and a person's hearing, sight, and skin will testify against them. When the sinners ask their skins why they testified, the skins will reply: 'Allah gave us speech as He has given speech to everything.'

title: The Weight of the Shahadah
question: What is the Hadith of the Bitaqah (the piece of paper)?
notes_sources: A man will have 99 massive scrolls of sins weighed against a single piece of paper containing the Shahadah. The scrolls will become light and the paper heavily outweigh them, proving that nothing can compare in weight with the sincere Name of Allah.

title: Conveying Salaam for Another
question: How do you reply when someone says 'Give my Salaam to so-and-so'?
notes_sources: The receiver must faithfully convey the greeting. When the intended person receives the greeting, they are required to reply by acknowledging both the sender and the conveyer, saying: 'Peace be upon you and him' (Alayka wa Alayhis-Salam).

title: Replying to Written Salaam
question: Is it mandatory to reply to a Salaam written in a letter or message?
notes_sources: Yes, it is compulsory. Because it is Wajib to reply to a Salaam immediately, it is recommended to give a verbal reply to the Salaam as soon as you read it, and then it is also proper to send a written reply back.

title: Interrupting Worship with Greetings
question: Should you say Salaam to someone engaged in Zikr or reciting the Quran?
notes_sources: It is strictly disallowed to say Salaam to a person deeply engaged in Zikr, reciting the Quran, or waiting for congregational prayer. It is not an occasion for greetings, as it distracts them from their worship.

title: Supplication for Transport
question: What should be recited when boarding a vehicle or mount?
notes_sources: One should say Bismillah, then Alhamdulillah, and glorify Allah who has provided the transportation in our control, acknowledging that we must ultimately return to our Lord in the Hereafter.

title: Drinking in Breaths
question: What is the Sunnah method of drinking water?
notes_sources: One should drink with the right hand, seated, and recite Bismillah. It is forbidden to gulp it down in a single continuous breath like a camel; rather, it should be drunk in two or three sips, physically separating the vessel from the mouth to breathe each time.

title: The Number of Beddings
question: What did the Prophet advise regarding excess beds in a home?
notes_sources: A Muslim should reasonably have up to three beddings: one for himself, one for his wife, and a third for a guest. Having a fourth unnecessary bedding is prohibited and is said to be 'for Satan,' as it promotes extravagance and waste.

title: Adorning Oneself for the Mosque
question: Is it important to dress well when going to the Masjid?
notes_sources: Yes. It is highly encouraged to beautify oneself when attending the mosque out of reverence for Allah's house. Being unconcerned about one's appearance, wearing pajamas, or wearing tight sports apparel that reveals body shapes is a significant error.

title: The Wearing of the Imamah
question: What is the virtue of wearing a turban (Imamah)?
notes_sources: Wearing the Imamah over a cap is a practice that historically distinguished Muslims. It is considered a perpetual Sunnah, and traditions state that the Angels send salutations upon those who wear an Imamah on Fridays.

title: The Steadfastness of Bilal
question: How did Bilal ibn Rabah resist torture in Makkah?
notes_sources: While being tortured with heavy rocks on his chest under the scorching sun, he fiercely refused to praise the idols. Instead, to mock his executioners and buy his soul, he constantly chanted 'Ahad... Ahad' (One... One), maintaining unbreakable conviction.

title: The Falcon of Uhud
question: Which Companion was praised for fulfilling his pledge of martyrdom while still walking the earth?
notes_sources: Talhah ibn Ubaidullah. The Prophet pointed to him after reciting the verse about men who fulfilled their pledges to Allah, highlighting his immense bravery, sacrifice, and physical defense of the Prophet at the Battle of Uhud.

title: The Compiler of the Quran
question: Who was given the massive responsibility of physically compiling the Quran?
notes_sources: Zaid ibn Thaabit. He meticulously and eagerly compiled the scattered written verses of the Holy Quran from various materials into a single unified book, an accomplishment for which he deserves the eternal gratitude of the Ummah.

title: Seeking Rain through Al-Abbaas
question: Who did Umar ask to supplicate for rain during the Year of Drought?
notes_sources: 'Umar took Al-Abbaas, the Prophet's uncle, and supplicated to Allah for rain for his sake, recognizing his venerable status and close blood relationship to the Prophet. The congregation did not leave before heavy rain poured.

title: Good Books as Companions
question: How does reading beneficial books aid one's psychological well-being?
notes_sources: Engaging with a beneficial book drives away anxiety, prevents one from delving into useless or sinful matters, and nourishes the soul with profound concepts. It serves as a companion that improves character, intellect, and peace of mind.

title: The Dangers of Violent Games
question: How can violent entertainment harm a Muslim's mind?
notes_sources: Exposing the mind to excessively violent media and video games exposes sensitive minds to cruelty, desensitizes them to bloodshed, and wastes immense amounts of precious time, destroying worldly productivity and focus on the Hereafter.

title: The Pivot of the Deen
question: Why is 'enjoining good and forbidding evil' so fundamental?
notes_sources: It is the pivot of Islam and the primary reason Prophets were sent. If this principle is abandoned, the religion fades away, misguidance and corruption prevail, civilizations decline, and entire nations are ultimately destroyed.

title: Expressions of Joy for the Prophet's Birth
question: How can a believer appropriately express joy for the coming of the Prophet?
notes_sources: Believers can show love and joy for the Prophet's birth by displaying permissible decorations (like flags or lights), feeding the poor, gathering to recite Na'ts, and reading about his life, provided it strictly avoids intermingling, blocking traffic, or violating Shari'ah.
